title: 322: East Germany: Life Behind the Iron Curtain

sentences.en: So Tom Holland, that was a national anthem and 10 points to you if you can guess which anthem it was.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德，那是一首国歌，如果你能猜出是哪一首，我就给你加10分。

sentences.en: I thought you just tuned into Radio 3.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你刚调到了BBC广播三台。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: It sounded kind of like generic, slightly boring Radio 3 music.
sentences.zh: 听起来就像那种平庸、有点无聊的广播三台音乐。

sentences.en: I think that's very harsh.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你这话太刻薄了。

sentences.en: That is one of my favourite national antheMs.
sentences.zh: 那可是我最喜欢的国歌之一。

sentences.en: It's the national anthem of the German Democratic Republic, East Germany as was.
sentences.zh: 那是德意志民主共和国，也就是曾经的东德的国歌。

sentences.en: A country that Tom, you and I would have taken completely for granted.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那是一个你我曾经都觉得理所当然的国家。

sentences.en: When we were growing up, yes.
sentences.zh: 我们成长过程中确实如此。

sentences.en: When we were growing up as a fixture on the sporting map.
sentences.zh: 在我们成长过程中，它是体育版图上的一个固定存在。

sentences.en: I mean, think about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你想想看。

sentences.en: The Olympics.
sentences.zh: 奥运会。

sentences.en: But also it was a sort of avatar, wasn't it, in the West?
sentences.zh: 但它在西方也是一种象征，不是吗？

sentences.en: But also a fixture in spy novels.
sentences.zh: 而且它还是间谍小说里的常客。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: It was a sort of shorthand for the Iron Curtain.
sentences.zh: 它是“铁幕”的一种代名词。

sentences.en: The Iron Curtain, Warsaw Pact, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 铁幕、华约组织，诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But now completely gone.
sentences.zh: 但现在已经完全消失了。

sentences.en: And therefore one with Nineveh and Tyre.
sentences.zh: 因此它也像尼尼微和泰尔一样成为了历史。

sentences.en: And therefore very much a suitable subject for a history podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常适合作为历史播客的主题。

sentences.en: And fortunately, Dominic, we have just the person with us, don't we?
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，多米尼克，我们正好请到了合适的人选，不是吗？

sentences.en: Who can tell us about East Germany?
sentences.zh: 能为我们讲述东德历史的人。

sentences.en: We do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Long-term listeners to the rest of this issue.
sentences.zh: 本节目的长期听众。

sentences.en: We'll remember when we did Bismarck and Bismarck's Reich, the second German Reich.
sentences.zh: 应该还记得我们做过俾斯麦和俾斯麦帝国，也就是德意志第二帝国的那期节目。

sentences.en: And we had a wonderful guest called Katja Hoyer, who it turns out, Tom, is, or at least was, an East German.
sentences.zh: 当时我们请到了一位出色的嘉宾卡佳·霍耶，结果发现，汤姆，她本人就是，或者至少曾经是东德人。

sentences.en: So Katja, not were you an East German, but you have now written the book on East Germany, which is Beyond the Wall, East Germany, 1949 to 1990.
sentences.zh: 所以卡佳，你不仅是东德人，现在还写了一本关于东德的书，书名是《墙外：东德，1949年至1990年》。

sentences.en: So this book's a bit different from your last one.
sentences.zh: 这本书和你上一本有点不同。

sentences.en: This is a bit more of a personal book, I guess, because it's about your own upbringing, actually features at the end of the book, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这更像是一本带有个人色彩的书，因为它讲述了你自己的成长经历，而且在书的结尾部分确实有所体现，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I did write it as a historian rather than as a personal history of the GDr.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我写这本书时是以历史学家的身份，而不是以东德个人史的角度。

sentences.en: But you can't ever quite sort of get away from your own personal background as a historian, I feel.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉，作为历史学家，你永远无法完全摆脱自己的个人背景。

sentences.en: So I felt obviously I had to be A, honest about the fact that I am from East Germany and that this is going to colour my perspective of the country to some extent.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，首先，我必须诚实地承认我来自东德，这在一定程度上会影响我对这个国家的看法。

sentences.en: And B, I didn't see why I shouldn't bring in my own kind of perspective,
sentences.zh: 其次，我不明白为什么我不能引入自己的视角，

sentences.en: my own family as part of the group of people that I bring into the mix in terms of explaining what the country was like from the perspective of those who lived there.
sentences.zh: 将我自己的家庭作为我所描述的群体的一部分，以此来解释那些生活在东德的人眼中的国家是什么样的。

sentences.en: So Katja, in your book, you have a very striking formulation.
sentences.zh: 卡佳，在你的书中，有一个非常引人注目的观点。

sentences.en: You say that the GDR, so East Germany, was unique among the Eastern Bloc nations in that its very existence was never assured.
sentences.zh: 你说东德在东欧集团国家中是独一无二的，因为它的存在从未得到过保障。

sentences.en: So the other Warsaw Pact nations, Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, whatever, I mean, these are kind of nation states.
sentences.zh: 其他的华约国家，比如波兰、罗马尼亚、保加利亚等等，它们算是民族国家。

sentences.en: But the whole thing about East Germany is that actually it's carved out of the Third Reich.
sentences.zh: 但东德的特殊之处在于，它实际上是从第三帝国中切割出来的。

sentences.en: And the question of whether it should ever have existed in the first place is hugely debated, not just by Germans, not just by people in the West, but also I learned from Stalin.
sentences.zh: 关于它最初是否应该存在的问题，不仅在德国人、西方人之间，甚至据我所知，在斯大林那里也存在巨大的争议。

sentences.en: So its origins lie in that kind of massive, massive catastrophe that overwhelms Germany over the course of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 所以它的起源在于20世纪席卷德国的那场巨大灾难。

sentences.en: So how far back do the roots of East Germany run back to the Third Reich, back to the Russian Revolution?
sentences.zh: 那么东德的根源可以追溯到多远？是追溯到第三帝国，还是追溯到俄国革命？

sentences.en: How far back does it go?
sentences.zh: 它到底能追溯到多远？

sentences.en: Well, they certainly when later they rediscovered sort of, you know, Prussia and Martin Luther and other things, they thought it went way further back.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当后来他们重新发现普鲁士、马丁·路德和其他事物时，他们认为可以追溯到更久远以前。

sentences.en: But of course, that was a means of legitimizing the fact that there was this fairly artificial line drawn in the middle of Germany after the Second World War,
sentences.zh: 但当然，那只是为了让二战后在德国中部划出的那条相当人为的界线合法化，

sentences.en: which is entirely a political decision, a decision based on where troops were at the time when they occupied Germany.
sentences.zh: 那完全是一个政治决定，一个基于当时占领德国的军队位置所做出的决定。

sentences.en: And it's certainly not a kind of natural line that evolved over centuries, as you find with many other countries.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是像许多其他国家那样经过几个世纪演变而成的自然界线。

sentences.en: And because of that, you basically have a country, one nation now split into two, which will naturally try and revert to some form of unity, national unity.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，你基本上拥有一个国家，一个现在分裂成两个的国家，它自然会试图恢复某种形式的统一，即民族统一。

sentences.en: And on the other side, you've got, you know, Stalin sitting there, not really keen on the idea that East Germany is part of this realm that he has to look after,
sentences.zh: 而在另一边，你知道，斯大林坐在那里，并不太热衷于让东德成为他必须照看的领土的一部分，

sentences.en: because it doesn't, in his view, fit into this kind of natural sphere of influence that Russia deems Eastern Europe to be, the Slavic people, effectively.
sentences.zh: 因为在他看来，它并不符合俄罗斯所认为的东欧——即斯拉夫民族——那种自然的势力范围。

sentences.en: So Germany is always going to be, from a Russian perspective, part of the Western world, part of Western Europe,
sentences.zh: 所以从俄罗斯的角度来看，德国永远是西方世界、西欧的一部分，

sentences.en: and therefore not necessarily a natural part of the sort of Soviet empire or the kind of, more widely speaking, the kind of Russian influence in Europe.
sentences.zh: 因此它不一定是苏联帝国，或者更广泛地说，不一定是俄罗斯在欧洲影响力范围内的自然组成部分。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, there are various considerations across the early period of the GDR, certainly, where the Soviets are basically thinking, can we trade this in?
sentences.zh: 结果就是，在东德早期的各个阶段，苏联人基本上都在考虑：我们能把它交易出去吗？

sentences.en: And is it really worth having?
sentences.zh: 它真的值得拥有吗？

sentences.en: And so the GDR government is constantly going to look East and West for justification for its own existence.
sentences.zh: 因此，东德政府不断地向东西方寻求其自身存在的正当性。

sentences.en: I was amazed to learn that.
sentences.zh: 听到这个我感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: I had no idea that Stalin was so reluctant and that essentially the drive for it comes from German communists, is that right?
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道斯大林竟然如此勉强，而且东德的建立本质上是源于德国共产主义者的推动，是这样吗？

sentences.en: And principally, German communists who had fled the Nazis and gone to Russia and survived all the various purges, which claimed the lives of many German communists,
sentences.zh: 主要是那些逃离纳粹并前往俄罗斯，且在清洗中幸存下来的德国共产主义者，这些清洗夺去了许多德国共产主义者的生命，

sentences.en: and who had been kind of battle-hardened and forged into becoming the most loyal of the loyal, as far as Stalin was concerned.
sentences.zh: 他们经过了战火的洗礼，在斯大林看来，他们成为了最忠诚的人。

sentences.en: And so they were able to essentially kind of pressure him and say, you know, we're here for you.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上能够向他施压，说，你知道，我们是为你效力的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that is an interesting fact that is often forgotten when you think, you know, out of the Communist Party's leadership that go to Russia to flee Hitler's regime,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是一个有趣的事实，当你想到那些为了逃避希特勒政权而前往俄罗斯的共产党领导层时，往往会被遗忘，

sentences.en: at the end of the war, only two of them are left standing, literally, and that's Willem Peek, who will become the first and only president of the GDR,
sentences.zh: 战争结束时，他们中只有两人幸存下来，一个是威廉·皮克，他后来成为东德第一任也是唯一一任总统，

sentences.en: and Walter Albrecht, who will sort of lead its fortune for the first two decades.
sentences.zh: 另一个是瓦尔特·乌布利希，他领导了东德前二十年的命运。

sentences.en: And that's not a coincidence that those people survived, while others didn't.
sentences.zh: 这些人能幸存下来而其他人没有，这并非巧合。

sentences.en: And at the same time, you now have a situation, I mean, the fact that Stalin is reluctant is my opinion, and many other historians think the same way.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你现在面临的情况是，斯大林的勉强态度是我的观点，许多其他历史学家也持同样的看法。

sentences.en: There are historians, I should point out, who don't think this, and who think that Stalin was always keen to hold on to East Germany and go as far into Western Europe as he could.
sentences.zh: 我应该指出，也有一些历史学家不这么认为，他们认为斯大林一直渴望控制东德，并尽可能深入西欧。

sentences.en: He's notoriously hard to pin down because he's so waffly in the way that he expresses his own opinion, so reluctant to have them kind of written in documents,
sentences.zh: 他以难以捉摸而闻名，因为他在表达自己的观点时总是含糊其辞，非常不愿意将这些观点写进文件中，

sentences.en: that it's really hard to sort of grasp what he actually wants from one moment to the next.
sentences.zh: 所以真的很难把握他从一刻到下一刻到底想要什么。

sentences.en: But there is this odd admiration for Germany as well, that he's got kind of like a love-hate relationship with Germany,
sentences.zh: 但背景中也存在着一种对德国的奇怪钦佩，他与德国之间有一种爱恨交织的关系，

sentences.en: and the idea that he should look after something that he, to some extent, views as a kind of another great European power,
sentences.zh: 而且他认为自己应该照顾某种在某种程度上被他视为另一个伟大的欧洲强国的东西，

sentences.en: it's not to be a satellite state as such, is also there in the background, I think.
sentences.zh: 它不应该仅仅是一个卫星国，这种想法我认为也存在于背景中。

sentences.en: And there are people in this inner circle, you've got people like Beria, for example,
sentences.zh: 在他的核心圈子里也有人，比如贝利亚，

sentences.en: the notorious sort of chief of the secret police, who doesn't view the GDR as a proper country.
sentences.zh: 那个臭名昭著的秘密警察头子，他不认为东德是一个真正的国家。

sentences.en: He says that quite openly and says, you know, what is this thing, if we're not looking after it, it would just crumble into West Germany, and there are constant considerations.
sentences.zh: 他很公开地说，你知道，这是什么东西？如果我们不照看它，它就会崩溃并融入西德，这种考虑一直存在。

sentences.en: All the trouble, you know, all the troops that have to go into it at the front lines of the Cold War, the awkward situation in Berlin with the open city that's split into two,
sentences.zh: 所有的麻烦，你知道，所有必须部署在冷战前线的军队，柏林作为分裂成两半的开放城市的尴尬处境，

sentences.en: all of that is there on people's minds, and the question is always there, should we not just give in and, you know, leave it?
sentences.zh: 所有这些都在人们的脑海中，问题始终存在：我们难道不应该放弃并离开它吗？

sentences.en: To go back to the leaders, so you mentioned Wilhelm Pieck and Walter Ulbricht, who were the sort of founding fathers of the GDR, and they had been in Moscow in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 回到领导人身上，你提到了威廉·皮克和瓦尔特·乌布利希，他们是东德的开国元勋，他们在20世纪30年代曾在莫斯科。

sentences.en: How much do you think the tone of political life in East Germany was shaped by the fact that they'd been in the purges, in the terror?
sentences.zh: 你认为东德政治生活的基调在多大程度上受到了他们经历过清洗和恐怖的影响？

sentences.en: Do you think that hung over the country right through to the very end?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种阴影是否一直笼罩着这个国家直到最后？

sentences.en: How much was that sense of mistrust and the sort of the lives of others sort of tone of East German life
sentences.zh: 那种不信任感，以及我们在西方所熟悉的东德生活中那种“他人的生活”般的基调，

sentences.en: that we're familiar with in the West, because that's become our stereotype of East Germany?
sentences.zh: 因为那已经成为了我们对东德的刻板印象，

sentences.en: How much was that dictated by the fact that they had been there in the 30s?
sentences.zh: 在多大程度上是由他们曾在30年代经历过那些事所决定的？

sentences.en: Or would that have been there anyway?
sentences.zh: 还是说即使没有这些，那种基调也会存在？

sentences.en: Because, Katja, you give the amazing statistic that only a quarter of German exiles in Russia survived the purges.
sentences.zh: 因为卡佳，你给出了一个惊人的统计数据，只有四分之一在俄罗斯的德国流亡者在清洗中幸存下来。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is really quite amazing when you think about this, and the amount of terror and kind of, you know, the psychological impact that this would have had
sentences.zh: 是的，当你想到这一点时，确实非常令人震惊，而且这种恐怖以及他们作为个人所承受的心理影响，

sentences.en: on these people as individuals, I think it's hard to underestimate.
sentences.zh: 我认为怎么估计都不为过。

sentences.en: When you think further back as well, they've always been persecuted for who they were politically, for where they stood.
sentences.zh: 当你进一步回溯时，你会发现他们一直因为自己的政治立场而受到迫害。

sentences.en: You know, you've got before the First World War, you've got very kind of harsh anti-social democratic, anti-socialist laws coming into place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在第一次世界大战之前，就有非常严厉的反社会民主党、反社会主义法律出台。

sentences.en: Then many of them sat in prison during the First World War for their opposition to it.
sentences.zh: 然后许多人在第一次世界大战期间因为反对战争而入狱。

sentences.en: And then throughout the 1920s, they had, you know, these hefty street battles on the streets of the Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪20年代，他们在魏玛共和国的街头进行了激烈的街头斗争。

sentences.en: And then Hitler obviously drives that to a whole new level.
sentences.zh: 然后希特勒显然将这种迫害推向了一个全新的高度。

sentences.en: And suddenly they run away from all of that.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们逃离了这一切。

sentences.en: And they end up in a situation that's even more deadly.
sentences.zh: 结果却陷入了一个更加致命的境地。

sentences.en: I mean, if you're German and you're in Russia during the Second World War, it's more likely that you will be dead at the end of the war than alive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你是德国人，并且在第二次世界大战期间身处俄罗斯，那么战争结束时你死亡的可能性比活着的可能性更大。

sentences.en: And coming out of all of that, a lifetime's worth of persecution, if you will, or looking over your shoulder for people that have got it in for you,
sentences.zh: 经历了这一切，可以说是一辈子的迫害，或者总是提防着那些想对付你的人，

sentences.en: has got to have some sort of political impact, I think, on the way that you act, that you set up a state.
sentences.zh: 我认为这必然会对你的行为方式以及你建立国家的方式产生某种政治影响。

sentences.en: And this goes for people like Eric Milker, who, for instance, fought in the, was deployed in the Spanish Civil War as a kind of underground terrorist, if you will.
sentences.zh: 这适用于像埃里希·米尔克这样的人，例如，他曾作为某种地下恐怖分子被部署在西班牙内战中。

sentences.en: So again, constantly looking over the shoulder for enemies.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，总是要提防敌人。

sentences.en: Eric Milker is the guy who goes on to found the Stasi, the secret police.
sentences.zh: 埃里希·米尔克就是后来创立秘密警察机构“斯塔西”的那个人。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And with that, kind of Russia as a role model in mind.
sentences.zh: 而且是以俄罗斯为榜样。

sentences.en: So he openly calls his staff, for instance, the Czechos, after the Russian secret police.
sentences.zh: 所以他公开称他的员工为“契卡”，这是以俄罗斯秘密警察命名的。

sentences.en: But also with his experiences in Russia in mind, where he actually witnessed some of the show trials that were going on under Stalin.
sentences.zh: 但这也是基于他在俄罗斯的经历，他亲眼目睹了斯大林统治下的一些作秀审判。

sentences.en: So in many ways, I think, you know, people don't come out of nowhere in 1949 with no background.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，我认为人们并不是在1949年凭空出现的，他们是有背景的。

sentences.en: And that, I think, plays into the early years, certainly, of the GDr.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这无疑影响了东德的早期岁月。

sentences.en: And because the personnel doesn't really change, I mean, Eric Milker is there to the very end in 1989.
sentences.zh: 而且因为人事并没有真正改变，我的意思是，埃里希·米尔克一直待到1989年最后时刻。

sentences.en: You've also got Eric Honecker, who leads the GDR for the second half of his existence, who also sat in Nazi prisons for years on end.
sentences.zh: 还有埃里希·昂纳克，他在东德存在的后半段领导着这个国家，他也曾在纳粹监狱里坐了多年牢。

sentences.en: So in many ways, you know, you don't get a fresh generation of people in that have grown up during kind of a relatively peaceful era with less psychological baggage.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，你并没有得到一代在相对和平时代成长起来、心理负担较轻的新人。

sentences.en: So just on the foundation of the GDR, I mean, Tom was asking that question about Stalin,
sentences.zh: 关于东德的建立，汤姆刚才问了关于斯大林的问题，

sentences.en: which I also found fascinating, because I had always imagined that the decision to create a separate state
sentences.zh: 我也觉得很迷人，因为我一直以为建立一个独立国家的决定，

sentences.en: was largely inspired from Moscow rather than from within the future East German state itself.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是受莫斯科的启发，而不是来自未来东德国家内部本身。

sentences.en: So is there a future?
sentences.zh: 那么，还有未来吗？

sentences.en: Is there an alternative universe in which there is a united Germany going into the 1950s?
sentences.zh: 是否存在一个平行的宇宙，在那里有一个统一的德国进入20世纪50年代？

sentences.en: Or do you think that the way that the Second World War ended, with the country split in two, the Red Army in one bit, the British, the Americans in another,
sentences.zh: 还是你认为第二次世界大战结束的方式，国家一分为二，红军占领一部分，英美占领另一部分，

sentences.en: do you think that meant the creation of East Germany was always inevitable?
sentences.zh: 你认为这意味着东德的建立始终是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: Well, as historians, we don't really like the idea of inevitability, I guess.
sentences.zh: 嗯，作为历史学家，我们不太喜欢“不可避免”这个概念。

sentences.en: But it's hard to see how a united Germany could have come out of this, because both sides, you know, due to its sheer size and weight,
sentences.zh: 但很难看出一个统一的德国如何能从这种局面中产生，因为双方，你知道，由于其巨大的体量和分量，

sentences.en: there couldn't have been an Austrian kind of scenario where you end up with a neutral country that won't get involved in anything.
sentences.zh: 不可能出现像奥地利那样的局面，即最终成为一个不参与任何事务的中立国。

sentences.en: I think that just doesn't work for where Germany is, for how big it is, for how much potential it has.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于德国所处的位置、它的大小以及它所拥有的潜力来说是行不通的。

sentences.en: I don't think it's ever possible to have a neutral Germany in the centre of Europe.
sentences.zh: 我不认为在欧洲中心拥有一个中立的德国是可能的。

sentences.en: And so it would have been, you know, even if you had it just for a short term, it would have been a playground for spies, undercover operations.
sentences.zh: 所以即使你只是短期内拥有它，它也会成为间谍和秘密行动的温床。

sentences.en: People would have tried to influence the government elections, political parties from both sides.
sentences.zh: 人们会试图从双方影响政府选举和政党。

sentences.en: And I think it would have been unsustainable in the long run.
sentences.zh: 我认为从长远来看，这是不可持续的。

sentences.en: I mean, you would have shifted, obviously, the Cold War with the Iron Curtain, effectively further eaSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你显然会把冷战和铁幕有效地向东推移。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you know, would the Russians have allowed Germany to become West Germany, effectively?
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，俄罗斯人会允许德国成为西德吗？

sentences.en: And it would have possibly happened.
sentences.zh: 这可能发生过。

sentences.en: You know, this kind of idea of Konrad Adenauer in the West, the first German, West German Chancellor,
sentences.zh: 你知道，西德第一任总理康拉德·阿登纳的这种想法，

sentences.en: pulling West Germany so far to the West that it becomes part of NATO and remilitarises very quickly.
sentences.zh: 把西德拉向西方，使其成为北约的一部分并迅速重新武装。

sentences.en: That would have scared, you know, Stalin to a point where he couldn't have accepted that.
sentences.zh: 那会把斯大林吓到他无法接受的地步。

sentences.en: So I don't really see how it would have been possible to have one unified Germany without one side or the other trying to grasp it for themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的看不出在没有一方试图将其据为己有的情况下，如何可能拥有一个统一的德国。

sentences.en: And so Volta Ulbricht, who I was delighted to read from you, had an unusually high pitch.
sentences.zh: 关于瓦尔特·乌布利希，我很高兴读到你写的，他的音调异常高。

sentences.en: So very high pitched voice.
sentences.zh: 嗓音非常尖细。

sentences.en: He said that of the state that he and his fellow communists were planning to set up, it has to look democratic, but we must have everything in our hands.
sentences.zh: 他说，他和他的共产主义同僚计划建立的国家，必须看起来是民主的，但我们必须把一切掌握在自己手中。

sentences.en: So that's a kind of cynical approach.
sentences.zh: 这是一种愤世嫉俗的方法。

sentences.en: It's like he's in the room, Tom.
sentences.zh: 就像他就在房间里一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Oh, well, thank you, Katja.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，谢谢你，卡佳。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you also have a fair measure of brutality.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你也面临着相当程度的残酷。

sentences.en: So the Soviets are looting a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 苏联人掠夺了很多东西。

sentences.en: They're looting a lot of kind of the industrial base.
sentences.zh: 他们掠夺了大量的工业基础。

sentences.en: They're looting prehistoric gold treasures, all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他们掠夺了史前金银财宝，各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: And people are going in and removing all the Junkers, the kind of the Prussian aristocrats.
sentences.zh: 人们进去并清除了所有的容克贵族，也就是普鲁士贵族。

sentences.en: They're being kicked off their land.
sentences.zh: 他们被赶出了自己的土地。

sentences.en: It's all being collectivized, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 一切都被集体化了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of familiar story from other East European countries.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个在其他东欧国家中很熟悉的故事。

sentences.en: And indeed, actually, from Germany under the Nazis, it's the combination of kind of democratic approach combined with violence.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在纳粹统治下的德国也是如此，这是民主手段与暴力相结合的产物。

sentences.en: Is that essentially how what becomes the GDR comes to be formed?
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是后来成为东德的国家的形成方式吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a lot of its origins go back to violence in various forms of repression as well.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为它的许多起源可以追溯到各种形式的暴力和压迫。

sentences.en: I mean, you have former Nazi concentration camps turned into what are now special Soviet camps, effectively.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你拥有前纳粹集中营，它们被改造成了现在的苏联特别营地。

sentences.en: And anybody who's vaguely associated with the Nazis, and we're talking a lot of people here, you know, party members, people that were in the Hitler Youth and so on and so forth,
sentences.zh: 任何与纳粹有丝毫关联的人，我们这里指的是很多人，你知道，党员、希特勒青年团成员等等，

sentences.en: end up in those camps.
sentences.zh: 最终被关进那些集中营里。

sentences.en: At the same time, as you say, there's lots of violence from the Soviet occupiers.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，正如你所说，苏联占领者也带来了大量的暴力。

sentences.en: That's looting on all sorts of levels.
sentences.zh: 那是一种全方位的掠夺。

sentences.en: I mean, it starts on the personal level with the proverbial bicycle being ripped out of people's hands and goes all the way up to, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它始于个人层面，比如众所周知的从人们手中抢走自行车，一直上升到，你知道的，

sentences.en: sort of organized looting from organized really by the state where they go into museums and clear them out, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 某种由国家组织的有组织掠夺，他们进入博物馆并将其洗劫一空，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And then, of course,
sentences.zh: 当然，还有，

sentences.en: you've got horrific violence towards the women and children that were largely left by themselves because the men were fighting still or in prisoner of war camps.
sentences.zh: 你还会看到对妇女和儿童的骇人听闻的暴力，她们大多被留在了家里，因为男人们还在打仗或者被关在战俘营里。

sentences.en: You know, it's estimated that two million women were raped, for example.
sentences.zh: 你知道，据估计有两百万妇女被强奸，例如。

sentences.en: So all of these things are going on and they collectively, I think, lead to a sort of foundation trauma on a personal level, on a psychological level,
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些事情都在发生，我认为它们共同导致了一种基础性的创伤，在个人层面、心理层面，

sentences.en: as well as on an economic level.
sentences.zh: 以及经济层面。

sentences.en: And that's something that the GDR has got to sort of try and recover from when the same level of violence does not apply to West Germany.
sentences.zh: 而当西德并没有遭受同样程度的暴力时，东德必须设法从中恢复过来。

sentences.en: Am I right in thinking that one thing that we would sometimes miss in this sort of Cold War historiography, if you like,
sentences.zh: 我这样想对吗：在冷战史学中，如果我们愿意这样称呼它的话，我们有时会忽略的一点是，

sentences.en: is that East Germany is not just born out of trauma and violence and repression and paranoia, but there's also a lot of idealism.
sentences.zh: 东德不仅仅诞生于创伤、暴力、压迫和偏执，其中也包含着许多理想主义。

sentences.en: So if you're young, let's say you're in the Hitler Youth, you're now in your teens, late teens or something.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你很年轻，比如说你在希特勒青年团，现在十几岁，快二十岁或者类似年纪。

sentences.en: So you've known all the promises that Hitler made to you.
sentences.zh: 你了解希特勒对你做出的所有承诺。

sentences.en: They've all turned out to be false.
sentences.zh: 结果证明它们全是谎言。

sentences.en: Society has fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 社会已经分崩离析。

sentences.en: And here are these guys who won the war, who beat you, and who are now saying, listen, a new world of freedom, of brotherhood, of internationalism, of equality.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这些赢得了战争、打败了你的人，正在说：听着，这是一个充满自由、兄弟情谊、国际主义和平等的新世界。

sentences.en: I mean, there are a lot of people who believe in that, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有很多人相信这一点，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not just imposed on them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不仅仅是强加给他们的。

sentences.en: There are people who willingly and enthusiastically go along with it.
sentences.zh: 有些人是自愿且热情地追随它。

sentences.en: Well, one of them is Angela Merkel's father, who's a pastor who goes from West Germany to live in East Germany.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中之一就是安格拉·默克尔的父亲，他是一位从西德搬到东德居住的牧师。

sentences.en: And Bertolt Brecht, the great playwright, does.
sentences.zh: 伟大的剧作家贝尔托·布莱希特也是如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And you get lots of people who believe that genuinely this is the new kind of Germany that hasn't been able to really found its foundation in the Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 你会发现很多人真心相信这就是魏玛共和国未能真正奠定基础的那种新德国。

sentences.en: So again, you know, we go back to broken promises.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们又回到了那些破碎的承诺。

sentences.en: That was another period where there was supposed to be real social change and social mobility and welfare and all of these kinds of inequality happening.
sentences.zh: 那是另一个本应实现真正社会变革、社会流动、福利以及消除所有这些不平等的时期。

sentences.en: And it didn't and it fell apart.
sentences.zh: 但它没有实现，反而分崩离析了。

sentences.en: And now there's this new Germany that is being set up.
sentences.zh: 而现在，一个新的德国正在建立。

sentences.en: And it did help that initially Stalin quite famously said that Hitler's come and go, but the German state remains.
sentences.zh: 而且，斯大林那句名言确实在初期起到了一定作用，他说希特勒来来去去，但德国国家长存。

sentences.en: You know, and this kind of idea that the Soviets were almost, despite all of the horrific stuff that happened and the great sacrifice that they made in the war,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种想法——尽管发生了所有可怕的事情，尽管他们在战争中做出了巨大的牺牲，苏联人几乎还是，

sentences.en: that they were sort of almost willing to see the German people as a separate thing from Nazism when the Western allies weren't quite willing to do that just yet,
sentences.zh: 几乎愿意将德国人民与纳粹主义区分开来看待，而西方盟国当时还不完全愿意这样做，

sentences.en: also gave people hope that things would maybe change.
sentences.zh: 这也给了人们事情可能会改变的希望。

sentences.en: I mean, I've got one example that springs to mind is a woman called Regina Faustmann,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我脑海中浮现的一个例子是一位名叫雷吉娜·福斯特曼的女性，

sentences.en: who I've got in my book just as an ordinary East German, basically, was a teenager at the time in her late teens and just really wanted to get going.
sentences.zh: 我在书中提到她只是一个普通的东德人，当时还是个十几岁的少女，真的只想有所作为。

sentences.en: I think she joined the Free German Youth straight away, once it was set up, you know, wanted to roll up her sleeve, collect scrap metal,
sentences.zh: 我想她一成立就立刻加入了自由德国青年团，你知道，想要卷起袖子，收集废金属，

sentences.en: start clearing the rubble away and sort of set up this new Germany that many people genuinely believed in.
sentences.zh: 开始清理瓦砾，并建立起许多人真心相信的这个新德国。

sentences.en: And presumably also, I mean, going from the 40s into the 50s, just the fact that there's a relative degree of normality must have generated both relief,
sentences.zh: 而且大概也是，从40年代进入50年代，仅仅是相对程度的正常化，一定既带来了宽慰，

sentences.en: but a certain sense of loyalty towards this kind of emergent communist state.
sentences.zh: 也对这种新兴的共产主义国家产生了一种忠诚感。

sentences.en: Yeah, although I think that was also one of its faults, that it couldn't provide that as quickly as the West could,
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管我认为这也是它的缺点之一，因为它无法像西方那样迅速地提供这种正常化，

sentences.en: where sort of economic stability due to the martial aid money effectively was able to be established a lot earlier than in East Germany.
sentences.zh: 西方的经济稳定由于马歇尔计划的资金，实际上比东德建立得早得多。

sentences.en: But at the same time, yes, people did feel that they were creating something and they also felt they were creating it themselves.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，是的，人们确实感到他们正在创造某种东西，而且他们也感到这是他们自己创造的。

sentences.en: You know, there was a kind of defiance against the idea that they were almost like three steps back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一种对“他们几乎落后了三步”这种观念的蔑视。

sentences.en: And now they had to fight for themselves and create their own country with their own hard graft, as it were.
sentences.zh: 现在他们必须为自己而战，用他们自己的辛勤劳动来建立自己的国家。

sentences.en: And that really had appealed to a lot of people as well.
sentences.zh: 这确实也吸引了很多人。

sentences.en: And at that point, so we're talking late 40s, early 50s, you can move quite freely from one Germany to the other.
sentences.zh: 在那时，也就是40年代末50年代初，你可以相当自由地从一个德国移动到另一个德国。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吗？

sentences.en: So in other words, if you want to get a new job or if you just say, golly, this, I hate this, communism not working.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你想找份新工作，或者你只是说，天哪，我讨厌这个，共产主义行不通。

sentences.en: You literally just pack your stuff in the car, if you have a car or you hitch or whatever, and you move 100 miles to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 你真的只需要把东西装进车里（如果你有车的话），或者搭便车什么的，然后搬到100英里外的西德。

sentences.en: And it's as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 就是这么简单。

sentences.en: Am I, is that, is that right?
sentences.zh: 我，这是，这是对的吗？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To start with, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 起初，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, they did pretty early on and mostly 1952 onwards beef up that inner, that long inner German border between the two states rather than the one in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实在很早的时候，主要是1952年以后，加强了两个国家之间那条漫长的德国内部边界，而不是柏林的那条。

sentences.en: But the Berlin one stays open until the Berlin Wall is erected.
sentences.zh: 但柏林的边界一直保持开放，直到柏林墙建立。

sentences.en: So there is that choice and many, many people take it.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有那种选择，而且很多人都做了。

sentences.en: That's one of the early challenges that this kind of young state and even the Soviet zone has got to cope with as well.
sentences.zh: 这是这个年轻的国家，甚至苏联占领区必须应对的早期挑战之一。

sentences.en: And so in the early 50s, you have a continual drain.
sentences.zh: 所以，在50年代初，你面临着持续的人才流失。

sentences.en: So we're talking about hundreds of thousands of people from East to WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是成千上万的人从东德流向西德。

sentences.en: And these are people who are anxious, presumably, it must be a combination of things.
sentences.zh: 这些人很焦虑，大概是因为多种因素的结合。

sentences.en: So is it, the economy must be part of it because the economy in the West is reviving more quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以，经济一定是其中的一部分，因为西方的经济复苏得更快。

sentences.en: But are people now beginning to think, so Tom was talking about the democratic means,
sentences.zh: 但人们现在是否开始思考，就像汤姆刚才谈到的民主手段，

sentences.en: they have this very strange electoral system where they basically print out all the names of the winners and then you put it in the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种非常奇怪的选举制度，基本上是把获胜者的名字印出来，然后你把它放进投票箱。

sentences.en: Yeah, also known as paper folding by the East German population.
sentences.zh: 是的，这在东德民众中也被称为“折纸”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: About that point, are people thinking, actually, this is a terrible sham.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，人们是否在想，实际上，这是一个可怕的骗局。

sentences.en: I've now seen through the lies.
sentences.zh: 我已经看穿了这些谎言。

sentences.en: I'm off.
sentences.zh: 我要走了。

sentences.en: I'm going to Frankfurt or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我要去法兰克福或者其他什么地方。

sentences.en: And also, you've got the Stasi, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 而且，你还有史塔西，不是吗？

sentences.en: So that's initiated in 1950.
sentences.zh: 那是1950年开始的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it comes very large, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且它很快就变得非常庞大。

sentences.en: So is that sense of oppression also something that people are fleeing?
sentences.zh: 那么，那种压迫感也是人们逃离的原因吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Although most of the evidence seems to point in the direction that economic factors seems to be, by a long way, the biggest pull.
sentences.zh: 尽管大多数证据似乎都指向经济因素在很大程度上是最大的吸引力。

sentences.en: Like the West German government, because they were overwhelmed with refugees,
sentences.zh: 就像西德政府，因为他们被难民淹没了，

sentences.en: both from East Germany and from the territories in Eastern Europe that Germany had lost after the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 既有来自东德的，也有来自二战后德国失去的东欧领土的。

sentences.en: So they set up sort of like refugee camps.
sentences.zh: 所以他们建立了类似难民营的地方。

sentences.en: And when people arrived there, they filled in surveys as to why they were there and what they wanted to do with their lives.
sentences.zh: 当人们到达那里时，他们会填写调查问卷，说明他们为什么在那里，以及他们想如何生活。

sentences.en: And the results of those show that, you know, the vast majority of people are there because they seek economic betterment.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，你知道，绝大多数人去那里是因为他们寻求经济改善。

sentences.en: And that's not just to say I'm earning a little bit more, but actually having goods on the shelves.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是说我多赚一点钱，而是实际上货架上有商品。

sentences.en: You know, the situation with food was still incredibly unstable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，食物供应的情况仍然极其不稳定。

sentences.en: East Germany had to keep rationing up much, much longer than West Germany did.
sentences.zh: 东德维持配给制的时间比西德长得多。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's this pretty fundamental economic stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这都是非常基础的经济问题。

sentences.en: And if people are wanting kind of secure conditions for themselves and their family, the West is a very attractive option,
sentences.zh: 如果人们想要为自己和家人寻求稳定的生活条件，西德是一个非常有吸引力的选择，

sentences.en: particularly if you have got a skill that's desperately needed in the rebuilding of Germany.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你拥有一项德国重建急需的技能。

sentences.en: So these are like, you know, skilled workers, for example, medical personnel, doctors, nurses,
sentences.zh: 所以这些人就像，你知道，熟练工人，例如，医疗人员、医生、护士，

sentences.en: those kinds of people who are really taken in with warm welcomes in the West and will find much, much more stable conditions there.
sentences.zh: 这类人在西德受到热烈欢迎，并且会在那里找到更加稳定的生活条件。

sentences.en: Just one quick thing about refugees.
sentences.zh: 关于难民，还有一件事。

sentences.en: Tom and I both have our hands up.
sentences.zh: 汤姆和我都在举手。

sentences.en: Please miss.
sentences.zh: 老师，请叫我。

sentences.en: Please miss.
sentences.zh: 老师，请叫我。

sentences.en: It says how interesting this topic is.
sentences.zh: 这说明这个话题有多么有趣。

sentences.en: So just on refugees, I was absolutely gobsmacked to read that a quarter of East Germany's population is made up of refugees who have fled, presumably from the former East Prussia,
sentences.zh: 关于难民，我非常震惊地读到，东德四分之一的人口是由难民组成的，他们大概是从前东普鲁士、

sentences.en: from the Sudetenland.
sentences.zh: 从苏台德地区逃出来的。

sentences.en: So that must be incredibly destabilizing.
sentences.zh: 那一定非常具有破坏性。

sentences.en: I mean, you're having to house all these people who have arrived from somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你必须安置所有这些从别处赶来的人。

sentences.en: And all the housing has been flattened by the, you know, by the Red Army.
sentences.zh: 而且所有的住房都被红军夷为平地了。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So there isn't enough housing stock to start with.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始就没有足够的住房存量。

sentences.en: It's just a sheer number.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是数量问题。

sentences.en: But you've got 12 to 14 million people fleeing those territories.
sentences.zh: 但你有1200万到1400万人逃离了那些领土。

sentences.en: And the vast majority of them arrived for geographical reasons alone, basically, in East Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们中的绝大多数人基本上仅仅因为地理原因就来到了东德。

sentences.en: My own family background, I've got three of my four grandparents come from there as well.
sentences.zh: 我自己的家庭背景，我的四个祖父母中有三个也来自那里。

sentences.en: East Prussia, Sudetenland and Pomerania, where, you know, they literally kind of walked for months, one of them years.
sentences.zh: 东普鲁士、苏台德和波美拉尼亚，他们真的走了好几个月，其中一个人走了好几年。

sentences.en: My grandfather only arrived in, I think, is 47.
sentences.zh: 我祖父直到我想是47年才到达。

sentences.en: So it did take a long time, basically, for people to get there.
sentences.zh: 所以人们到达那里确实花了很多时间。

sentences.en: And then they arrived somewhere where people didn't want them because they were struggling with their own conditions and there wasn't enough housing.
sentences.zh: 然后他们到达了一个人们不欢迎他们的地方，因为当地人也在为自己的生活条件挣扎，而且住房不足。

sentences.en: And then local authorities would say, well, you can move in with this farmer because he's got a barn somewhere that he isn't using.
sentences.zh: 然后地方当局会说，好吧，你可以搬去和这个农民住，因为他有个谷仓没在用。

sentences.en: And the farmer didn't really get a say in this.
sentences.zh: 而那个农民并没有什么发言权。

sentences.en: So, you know, people ended up basically working for free for a long time for the people that they were put up with.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，人们最终基本上是为收留他们的人免费工作了很长时间。

sentences.en: And the local school children wouldn't be particularly nice to you if you've just arrived from the EaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你刚从东边过来，当地的学童对你也不会特别友好。

sentences.en: So it wasn't a great situation to start with.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始情况并不好。

sentences.en: And I think one that's often underestimated in terms of how destabilising that is for society.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点在社会动荡程度方面经常被低估。

sentences.en: So all kinds of pressures, all kinds of tensions.
sentences.zh: 所以各种压力，各种紧张局势。

sentences.en: And in 1953, there is an uprising.
sentences.zh: 1953年，发生了起义。

sentences.en: So what's the story of that?
sentences.zh: 那么那段故事是怎样的？

sentences.en: What specifically precipitates it?
sentences.zh: 具体是什么引发了它？

sentences.en: And how does the German state, the East German state deal with that?
sentences.zh: 德国政府，即东德政府是如何处理的？

sentences.en: Well, they try to do too many things at once.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们试图同时做太多的事情。

sentences.en: You know, all of the problems that we just mentioned, on top of that, you've got a huge issue with energy in terms of actually producing heat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，除了我们刚才提到的所有问题之外，你在能源方面还有一个巨大的问题，即实际生产热能。

sentences.en: You know, brown coal really is the only thing that they've got, which is ridiculously inefficient and obviously quite bad for the environment as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，褐煤确实是他们唯一拥有的东西，它效率极低，而且显然对环境也非常有害。

sentences.en: But all of these things come at once.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些事情同时发生了。

sentences.en: And at the same time, Walter Ulbricht, the founding father of the GDR, if you will, presses ahead with this buildup of socialism program, which entails, for example,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，东德的开国元勋瓦尔特·乌布利希，如果你愿意这样称呼的话，推进了这个社会主义建设纲领，其中包含，例如，

sentences.en: a large restructuring or kind of reformation of the way that land is used.
sentences.zh: 对土地使用方式的大规模重组或某种改革。

sentences.en: So he takes away land from the Junkers, as you said earlier, but also from other sort of large farmers,
sentences.zh: 所以他从容克地主手中，正如你之前所说，也从其他一些大农场主手中夺走了土地，

sentences.en: cuts it up into small chunks and then gives it to all of these people who are called new farmers.
sentences.zh: 将其切分成小块，然后分给所有这些被称为“新农民”的人。

sentences.en: Effectively, people, for instance,
sentences.zh: 实际上，人们，例如，

sentences.en: those that come from the East are now given like sort of several football fields worth of land and it just isn't big enough to be used productively.
sentences.zh: 那些来自东部的人现在被分到了相当于几个足球场大小的土地，但它根本不够大，无法进行高效利用。

sentences.en: And therefore, the agricultural sector breaks down.
sentences.zh: 因此，农业部门崩溃了。

sentences.en: So there's all of this kind of stuff happening.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些事情都在发生。

sentences.en: Ideology clashes with the economic sort of realities on the ground and you end up with a situation where there's just not enough of anything.
sentences.zh: 意识形态与现实中的经济现实发生冲突，最终导致了一种什么都短缺的局面。

sentences.en: And on top of that, they're trying to build up the early sort of armed forces, security forces, police, Stasi.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他们试图建立早期的武装部队、安全部队、警察、史塔西。

sentences.en: They're trying to beef up the border from 1952 onwards.
sentences.zh: 他们试图从1952年开始加强边界。

sentences.en: It's just too much.
sentences.zh: 这实在是太多了。

sentences.en: And they're asking all of that of the workers and it becomes more and more and more work for less outcome.
sentences.zh: 他们要求工人做所有这些事情，结果工作越来越多，产出却越来越少。

sentences.en: And even the little money that you do get, you can't actually buy anything with it because there's nothing on the shelves.
sentences.zh: 即使你得到的那一点点钱，你也买不到任何东西，因为货架上什么都没有。

sentences.en: And so people are becoming incredibly unhappy.
sentences.zh: 所以人们变得非常不满。

sentences.en: They're looking west, you know, towards the economic miracle that's happening just across the border.
sentences.zh: 他们看向西方，你知道，看向就在边界对面发生的经济奇迹。

sentences.en: Many people have got relatives there who tell them how good everything is and how they've got all of the stability and the prosperity back.
sentences.zh: 许多人在那里有亲戚，他们告诉他们一切有多好，他们是如何恢复了所有的稳定和繁荣。

sentences.en: And they're just unhappy with this.
sentences.zh: 他们只是对现状感到不满。

sentences.en: And they see that this is partially caused by the actions of the regime.
sentences.zh: 而且他们看到这部分是由政权的行动造成的。

sentences.en: And hence, you get kind of a growing sense of anger, particularly amongst the working classes, which is somewhat ironic given that, you know, you have a workers and peasants state.
sentences.zh: 因此，你看到了一种日益增长的愤怒感，特别是在工人阶级中，考虑到你拥有的是一个“工农国家”，这多少有些讽刺。

sentences.en: It's a workers' paradise.
sentences.zh: 这是一个工人的天堂。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And so there's the summer of 1953, there's mass protests.
sentences.zh: 所以那是1953年的夏天，发生了大规模抗议。

sentences.en: So right about the 16th of June, it all sort of reaches a climax.
sentences.zh: 就在6月16日左右，一切都达到了高潮。

sentences.en: And I suppose the question is, at that point, why doesn't the East German regime fall?
sentences.zh: 我想问题是，在那个时候，为什么东德政权没有倒台？

sentences.en: Is it because there are enough people with a stake in the system?
sentences.zh: 是因为有足够多的人在这个体制中拥有利益吗？

sentences.en: Is it because they're backed up by the Red Army?
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们有红军撑腰吗？

sentences.en: What's the why doesn't why don't we have 1989 then in 1953?
sentences.zh: 那为什么1953年没有发生1989年那样的事呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, the main argument is that the Red Army intervened.
sentences.zh: 没错，我的意思是，主要论点是红军进行了干预。

sentences.en: They declare a state of emergency and literally roll in there with tanks and kind of battle hardened commanders and, you know, suppresses uprising brutally.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布进入紧急状态，直接开着坦克冲进去，带着那些久经沙场的指挥官，你知道的，残酷地镇压了起义。

sentences.en: I would say another reason is that many people just joined in.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个原因是很多人只是随大流加入了。

sentences.en: So many, many of the people that were there where, you know, I kind of listened to their testimony or looked at the evidence.
sentences.zh: 当时在场的人里有很多人，你知道，我听过他们的证词，也看过相关证据。

sentences.en: The overwhelming sense was, you know, I looked out of my window and there were people out there doing things and I was a bit unhappy as well.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人的感觉是，你知道，我从窗户往外看，外面有人在搞事情，我也觉得有点不爽。

sentences.en: So I went out and joined them.
sentences.zh: 所以我走出去加入了他们。

sentences.en: And those people immediately literally went back inside the moment the tanks rolled up and said, actually, I'm not that unhappy.
sentences.zh: 而那些人一看到坦克开过来，立刻就缩回屋里去了，说，其实我没那么不爽。

sentences.en: It'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 会没事的。

sentences.en: You know, and because straight after the Soviets basically said to Ulbricht, you need to sort this out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为苏联人紧接着基本上对乌布利希说，你得把这事处理好。

sentences.en: We told you beforehand, you can't build up socialism as quickly as you have done because it doesn't work and it destabilizes everything.
sentences.zh: 我们之前就告诉过你，你不能像现在这样搞这么快的社会主义建设，因为它行不通，而且会破坏一切稳定。

sentences.en: So essentially, Ulbricht is more communist than Stalin.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，乌布利希比斯大林还要共产主义。

sentences.en: He's more Stalinist than Stalin.
sentences.zh: 他比斯大林还要斯大林主义。

sentences.en: He's trying to prove to Stalin that he's more Stalinist than Stalin.
sentences.zh: 他是在向斯大林证明他比斯大林更像斯大林主义者。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Stalin was, you know, kind of the main point was to keep East Germany.
sentences.zh: 而斯大林，你知道，当时的核心重点是保住东德。

sentences.en: I mean, Stalin's obviously dead at this point, but the legacy of that remains.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，斯大林此时显然已经去世了，但那种遗产依然存在。

sentences.en: But if you have the situation where East Germany needs to be there for the Soviets to provide resources,
sentences.zh: 但如果你面临的情况是，东德必须存在，以便为苏联提供资源，

sentences.en: to pay reparations and to be exploited economically, and that doesn't work if your workers don't turn up and if the whole state erupts into chaos
sentences.zh: 支付赔款并被经济剥削，而如果你的工人们不干活，整个国家陷入混乱，那这一切就没法运作了，

sentences.en: and you have to send your own forces and your own resources in to help out.
sentences.zh: 而且你还得派遣自己的军队和资源去帮忙。

sentences.en: And this was what made the Soviets so reluctant to support this kind of really rapid and, you know, destructive buildup of socialism that Ulbricht is pursuing.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么苏联人如此不情愿支持乌布利希所追求的那种极其迅速且具有破坏性的社会主义建设。

sentences.en: And afterwards, after it happened, the Soviets said to them, well, you can stay here.
sentences.zh: 事后，在事情发生之后，苏联人对他们说，好吧，你们可以留在这里。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons is that Stalin had just died and Khrushchev, who's just emerging as the sort of successor,
sentences.zh: 原因之一是斯大林刚去世，而赫鲁晓夫，作为刚浮出水面的继任者，

sentences.en: doesn't want upheaval in East Germany whilst he's trying to deal with the zone upheaval in Russia.
sentences.zh: 在他试图处理俄罗斯国内动荡的同时，不希望东德也出现动荡。

sentences.en: They're saying to him, you need to now make sure that people have got decent living standards.
sentences.zh: 他们对他说，你现在必须确保人们有体面的生活水平。

sentences.en: Focus on that firSt. Everything else can come after.
sentences.zh: 先专注于这一点。其他一切都可以以后再说。

sentences.en: And Ulbricht is thereby forced to sort of take a step back from his buildup of socialism, allow a little bit of economic freedom.
sentences.zh: 因此，乌布利希被迫在社会主义建设上退了一步，允许了一点点经济自由。

sentences.en: And the Soviets are also sending truckloads, literally, of kind of foodstuffs and other things to try and help with the situation.
sentences.zh: 苏联人也确实运来了成卡车的食品和其他物资，试图帮助缓解局势。

sentences.en: It stabilises a bit.
sentences.zh: 局势稍微稳定了一些。

sentences.en: And repression is scared down as well.
sentences.zh: 镇压也减少了。

sentences.en: Because one of the points you make is that actually Ulbricht, after all his experiences with the Nazis and so on, has actually quite a deep mistrust of his compatriots.
sentences.zh: 因为你提到的观点之一是，乌布利希在经历了纳粹等等事情后，实际上对他的人民有着相当深的不信任。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't really trust them to do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他并不真正相信他们会做正确的事。

sentences.en: And so that's one of the reasons why there's such a measure of coercion in his kind of approach.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么他的那种方针中会有那么大程度的强制手段的原因之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, and he doesn't understand them either.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且他也不了解他们。

sentences.en: And I suppose in the long run, why the Iron Curtain and most notoriously the Berlin Wall in the end go up?
sentences.zh: 我想从长远来看，这就是为什么铁幕，以及最臭名昭著的柏林墙最终会竖起来的原因吧？

sentences.en: Because he can't rely on his fellow citizens in East Germany not to head WeSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他无法指望东德的公民不会逃往西方。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, one of the fundamental issues with him, and I would say with Honecker later as well, is that they weren't there during the war.
sentences.zh: 没错，我的意思是，他身上，以及后来昂纳克身上存在的一个根本问题是，他们在战争期间并不在那里。

sentences.en: They didn't understand what had happened in Germany for this entire period.
sentences.zh: 他们不了解这段时期德国到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And when you think how extreme Nazism is as an ideology, what it did to the country and the people that were there, weren't the same anymore.
sentences.zh: 当你想到纳粹主义作为一种意识形态是多么极端，它对这个国家做了什么，以及当时在那里的人们，他们已经不再是以前的他们了。

sentences.en: It's interesting as well when you look at, for instance, Wolfgang Leonard, who is one of the young communists who was sent back from Russia to Germany to build up socialism.
sentences.zh: 当你看看沃尔夫冈·莱昂哈德（Wolfgang Leonard）的例子也很有意思，他是被从俄罗斯送回德国建设社会主义的年轻共产党员之一。

sentences.en: He'd left Berlin as a teenager and then returned in 1945 to find that it's completely changed,
sentences.zh: 他十几岁时离开柏林，1945年回来时发现一切都变了，

sentences.en: not just physically, but that he doesn't get what people want, how they feel about things.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是物理上的，而是他根本不明白人们想要什么，他们对事情有什么感觉。

sentences.en: The fact that they feel that the Russians, as they called them, or the Moscovites coming back, didn't, they weren't proper Germans anymore.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们觉得这些所谓的“俄国人”，或者说回来的“莫斯科派”，已经不再是真正的德国人了。

sentences.en: They'd betrayed the country in some shape or form, or that was the feeling that people had.
sentences.zh: 他们以某种形式背叛了这个国家，或者这就是人们的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, they were totally disconnected.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们完全脱节了。

sentences.en: And the workers still want to talk in 1953 to Ulbricht.
sentences.zh: 而且工人们在1953年仍然想和乌布利希对话。

sentences.en: They walk up to his ministry and stand in front of it and say, come out and speak to us.
sentences.zh: 他们走到他的部门前，站在那里说，出来和我们谈谈。

sentences.en: And he just goes, oh, I think it's going to start raining soon.
sentences.zh: 而他只是说，哦，我想快要下雨了。

sentences.en: They'll soon go.
sentences.zh: 他们很快就会走的。

sentences.en: It'd be fine.
sentences.zh: 会没事的。

sentences.en: You know, it just shows how disconnected these people were from the people that they were trying to lead.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这恰恰表明这些人与他们试图领导的人民是多么脱节。

sentences.en: And I think that was one of the fundamental problems they never get rid of.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是他们从未摆脱的根本问题之一。

sentences.en: So it's a period of relative stability, the 50s, but there's a continuing drain.
sentences.zh: 所以50年代是一个相对稳定的时期，但人口流失一直在持续。

sentences.en: Then to deal with that drain of people, in 1961, they put up the Berlin Wall.
sentences.zh: 为了应对这种人口流失，1961年，他们竖起了柏林墙。

sentences.en: We did a podcast, didn't we, Tom, with Ian McGregor about the Berlin Wall.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们不是和伊恩·麦格雷戈（Ian McGregor）做过一期关于柏林墙的播客吗？

sentences.en: So one of the things you talk about the Berlin Wall that's quite sort of counterintuitive is the Berlin Wall actually, I mean, it freezes the situation, but it ensures stability.
sentences.zh: 所以关于柏林墙，你谈到的一点相当反直觉，那就是柏林墙实际上，我的意思是，它冻结了局势，但它确保了稳定。

sentences.en: So there's almost an argument, this will sound like an absolutely weird thing to say, but there's actually an argument to be made for the Berlin Wall in the sense that it means
sentences.zh: 所以几乎有一种论点，这听起来可能非常奇怪，但实际上确实有理由支持柏林墙，因为它意味着

sentences.en: that the sort of the threat of instability recedes.
sentences.zh: 那种不稳定的威胁消退了。

sentences.en: And actually, from the East German point of view, people just have to now knuckle down and make the best of the regime they have because there is no alternative.
sentences.zh: 实际上，从东德的角度来看，人们现在只能埋头苦干，利用他们现有的政权过好日子，因为别无选择。

sentences.en: Is that pretty much your view?
sentences.zh: 这基本上是你的观点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's certainly how it was viewed by most of the political leaders at the time.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，当时大多数政治领导人确实是这样看的。

sentences.en: You've got Ardenauer doing very, very little in West Germany about this, saying very little about it as well.
sentences.zh: 阿登纳在西德对此几乎什么都没做，对此也几乎只字未提。

sentences.en: The same goes for Kennedy, you know, and obviously, Orbit himself is happy in East Germany because it stabilises the situation.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪也是如此，你知道，显然，乌布利希本人在东德也很高兴，因为它稳定了局势。

sentences.en: But it's interesting how little kind of political resistance there is and also how little resistance there is on the ground.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，政治抵抗是多么少，而且基层的抵抗也如此之少。

sentences.en: I mean, yes, you do get a lot of unrest in Berlin itself, particularly actually more on the Western side than in East Berlin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，你在柏林本身确实看到了很多动荡，实际上西柏林比东柏林更多。

sentences.en: You do get that.
sentences.zh: 确实有这种情况。

sentences.en: But the rest of the country is surprisingly quiet.
sentences.zh: 但全国其他地方却出奇地安静。

sentences.en: And I asked almost all of the people I spoke to, you know, this is one of my key questions,
sentences.zh: 我问过我交谈过的几乎所有人，你知道，这是我的关键问题之一，

sentences.en: irrespective of what I actually wanted from them interview-wise.
sentences.zh: 不管我采访时真正想要得到什么。

sentences.en: Like, what did you make of the building of the Berlin Wall?
sentences.zh: 比如，你对柏林墙的修建有什么看法？

sentences.en: And the vast majority of them kind of shrugged their shoulders and said, well, I was on holiday.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人耸了耸肩说，嗯，我当时在度假。

sentences.en: I read about it in the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我在报纸上读到过。

sentences.en: I suppose it was quite good because our doctor now had to stay.
sentences.zh: 我想这挺好的，因为我们的医生现在必须留下来了。

sentences.en: But they had no particular feelings about it because they were working class people who had never travelled anywhere beforehand.
sentences.zh: 但他们对此没有任何特别的感觉，因为他们是从来没去过别处的工人阶级。

sentences.en: They lived in their communities where they always lived.
sentences.zh: 他们一直生活在他们一直居住的社区里。

sentences.en: And there was no possibility, whatever happened, you know, of them to move away and go somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 无论发生什么，他们都不可能搬走去别的地方。

sentences.en: So in many ways, it economically stabilised the situation.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，它在经济上稳定了局势。

sentences.en: And it also now meant that Ulbricht was put in a situation where he had to make life worthwhile in the GDR now that he'd locked people into it.
sentences.zh: 而且现在这也意味着乌布利希被置于一种境地，既然他已经把人们锁在里面，他就必须让东德的生活变得有价值。

sentences.en: And that in itself created a lot of social and economic change in the 60s because he had to ease the sort of tensions a little bit economically and try and build a stable country.
sentences.zh: 这本身就在60年代创造了大量的社会和经济变革，因为他必须在经济上稍微缓解一下紧张局势，并试图建立一个稳定的国家。

sentences.en: So the Berlin Wall has gone up.
sentences.zh: 所以柏林墙竖起来了。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we'll look at the decades between that and the Berlin Wall coming down again in 1989.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将看看从那之后到1989年柏林墙再次倒塌之间的几十年。

sentences.en: We'll look at trabants, fridges, steroids, all the kind of stuff that we associate with East
sentences.zh: 我们将看看卫星轿车、冰箱、类固醇，所有我们与东德联系在一起的东西。

sentences.en: Germany.
sentences.zh: 德国。

sentences.en: So we'll be back after the break.
sentences.zh: 所以休息后我们再回来。

sentences.en: East Berlin, 7th October 1989.
sentences.zh: 东柏林，1989年10月7日。

sentences.en: I was four years old, an excited little girl with unruly pitch black hair that resisted every attempt to control it.
sentences.zh: 我当时四岁，是一个兴奋的小女孩，留着一头不听话的乌黑头发，试图控制它的努力都失败了。

sentences.en: Wrapping my hands around the handrail of the rotating visitor platform of the Berlin television tower, I was straining forward to get as close to the panoramic glass panes
sentences.zh: 我双手抓着柏林电视塔旋转观景台的扶手，努力向前探身，尽可能靠近全景玻璃窗，

sentences.en: as I could.
sentences.zh: 尽可能地靠近。

sentences.en: I gazed down 203 metres at the streets below in amazement, trying to take it all in.
sentences.zh: 我惊奇地俯瞰着203米下方的街道，试图把这一切尽收眼底。

sentences.en: Delighted with the spectacle of Berlin from above, I turned around and shouted slightly too loudly, Papa, come and see.
sentences.zh: 被从高处俯瞰柏林的奇观所吸引，我转过身，声音稍微有点大地喊道：爸爸，快来看。

sentences.en: All those people look like little ants.
sentences.zh: 那些人看起来像小蚂蚁一样。

sentences.en: I pointed downwards eagerly, jumping up and down, so I could see better.
sentences.zh: 我急切地指着下方，跳上跳下，这样我能看得更清楚。

sentences.en: And look, there are police cars everywhere.
sentences.zh: 看，到处都是警车。

sentences.en: These last words made my father stop in his tracks.
sentences.zh: 这些最后的话让我父亲停下了脚步。

sentences.en: Looking down at the increasingly crowded square at the foot of the Fernsehtum, his face went white.
sentences.zh: 看着电视塔脚下越来越拥挤的广场，他的脸变得惨白。

sentences.en: He recognised the army of vehicles as belonging to paramilitary people's police units.
sentences.zh: 他认出那支车辆大军属于准军事化的人民警察部队。

sentences.en: Many of the people I was pointing at were protesters.
sentences.zh: 我指着的许多人都是抗议者。

sentences.en: So that was from Katja's new book, Beyond the Wall.
sentences.zh: 以上内容摘自卡佳（Katja）的新书《墙外》（Beyond the Wall）。

sentences.en: And Katja, that is your experience in 1989.
sentences.zh: 卡佳，那是你在1989年的经历。

sentences.en: Tom, so gallant of you to read that yourself, rather than to let Katja read her.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你亲自读那段真是太绅士了，而不是让卡佳自己读。

sentences.en: It's very weird watching Katja listen to you ventriloquising her.
sentences.zh: 看着卡佳听你替她配音，真是太奇怪了。

sentences.en: That's what we're all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们节目的特色。

sentences.en: It's a hall of mirrors, a hall of mirrors.
sentences.zh: 这是一个镜厅，一个镜厅。

sentences.en: So an amazing passage.
sentences.zh: 真是精彩的片段。

sentences.en: And it kind of introduces you as a character into the story that you're describing.
sentences.zh: 它把你作为一个角色引入了你所描述的故事中。

sentences.en: And it reminds, you know, it's kind of lived, vivid, personal history.
sentences.zh: 它提醒人们，你知道，这是一种鲜活的、生动的、个人的历史。

sentences.en: And we left the first episode, the Berlin Wall had been set up.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一集结束时，柏林墙已经建好了。

sentences.en: That's 1989, the downfall of the Berlin Wall.
sentences.zh: 那是1989年，柏林墙的倒塌。

sentences.en: Let's look at the decades between those two great events.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看这两大事件之间的几十年。

sentences.en: So first of all, the politics of it.
sentences.zh: 首先，关于它的政治。

sentences.en: Ulbricht is kind of hanging around like a slightly rotten smell.
sentences.zh: 乌布利希就像一股略带腐臭的气味一样徘徊不去。

sentences.en: But coming up on the outside track, we have Eric Honecker, who you mentioned before.
sentences.zh: 但在外围赛道上，我们有你之前提到的埃里希·昂纳克（Eric Honecker）。

sentences.en: And he also has a very high-pitched voice.
sentences.zh: 而且他的声音也很尖锐。

sentences.en: And additionally, he likes to mumble.
sentences.zh: 此外，他喜欢嘟囔。

sentences.en: So what is it about East German politicians and high-pitched voices?
sentences.zh: 那么东德政客和尖锐的嗓音之间有什么联系呢？

sentences.en: I think people forget to some extent that these, you know, they're not career politicians.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们在某种程度上忘记了，这些，你知道，他们不是职业政客。

sentences.en: They're sort of working-class people that come from fairly, you know, sort of down-to-earth, if you want to call it that,
sentences.zh: 他们是那种来自相当，你知道，相当脚踏实地，如果你想这么称呼它的话，

sentences.en: sort of backgrounds with no pretense of being particularly polished or particularly apt at kind of portraying a certain image in public.
sentences.zh: 那种背景的人，没有假装自己特别圆滑，或者特别擅长在公众面前塑造某种形象。

sentences.en: And they found it incredibly awkward at times to do just that.
sentences.zh: 他们有时发现做这些事情非常尴尬。

sentences.en: And especially Honecker, you see him a lot with, like, foreign politicians.
sentences.zh: 尤其是昂纳克，你经常看到他和外国政客在一起。

sentences.en: And he stands there almost shyly sort of wringing his hands or mumbling, you know, literally sort of, well, not literally, he hasn't got a beard, but mumbling into his beard.
sentences.zh: 他站在那里，几乎害羞地绞着双手，或者嘟囔着，你知道，字面上，嗯，不是字面上，他没有胡子，但对着他的胡子嘟囔。

sentences.en: It's easy to forget that these aren't people that come from a, like, well-bred and well-educated background.
sentences.zh: 很容易忘记这些人并非来自那种出身良好、受过良好教育的背景。

sentences.en: But, you know, they are a roofer and a carpenter.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他们是屋顶工和木匠。

sentences.en: And they come from backgrounds where you don't, you know, speak particularly eloquently or present yourself particularly confidently.
sentences.zh: 他们来自那种你不会，你知道，说话特别雄辩，或者表现得特别自信的背景。

sentences.en: And Honecker, fascinatingly, is not from the territory of East Germany.
sentences.zh: 而且昂纳克，有趣的是，他不是来自东德领土。

sentences.en: So he is from the West, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他是来自西德，对吧？

sentences.en: Where's he from?
sentences.zh: 他是哪里人？

sentences.en: Yeah, he's from the Saarland.
sentences.zh: 是的，他来自萨尔州（Saarland）。

sentences.en: And they naturally have kind of like a very soft accent.
sentences.zh: 他们天生就有一种非常柔和的口音。

sentences.en: It's hard to describe in English, but it lends itself to be rather difficult to understand.
sentences.zh: 用英语很难描述，但这种口音让人很难听懂。

sentences.en: Yeah, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 是的，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And he grows up with a pig, I gather, again, from your book, which is a wonderful detail.
sentences.zh: 而且我从你的书中了解到，他从小养了一头猪，这是一个很棒的细节。

sentences.en: And he comes in, so 1971, Ulbricht basically gets deposed, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他上台了，所以1971年，乌布利希基本上被罢免了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's kind of the Soviets lean on him and he gets pushed out.
sentences.zh: 苏联人向他施压，他就被挤走了。

sentences.en: And so Honecker comes in.
sentences.zh: 于是昂纳克上台了。

sentences.en: So Honecker made his name, well, not made his name, but Honecker in the 60s had been a great critic of the Beatles and of long hair and of youth.
sentences.zh: 昂纳克成名于，嗯，不是成名，但昂纳克在60年代曾是披头士乐队、长发和年轻人的大批评家。

sentences.en: So Honecker is the sort of, he's precisely the wrong person you could argue to take over, isn't he, in the early 70s?
sentences.zh: 所以昂纳克是那种，你可以说他是70年代初接管权力的最错误的人选，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's so backward looking and puritanical.
sentences.zh: 因为他太守旧和清教徒了。

sentences.en: But I thought that he was piling in and allowing all these German youth to buy jeans and things.
sentences.zh: 但我以为他当时正在投入并允许所有这些德国年轻人购买牛仔裤之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, those things are both true.
sentences.zh: 是的，这两件事都是真的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this is one of the things I find fascinating about the GDRs, just how much it oscillates between trying to open itself up and becoming more reformist
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这是我发现关于东德最迷人的事情之一，就是它在试图开放自己、变得更具改良主义，

sentences.en: and then drawing back in on itself.
sentences.zh: 和随后退缩回自身之间摇摆不定。

sentences.en: And I think that's reflected in both Ulbricht and Honecker.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在乌布利希和昂纳克身上都有所体现。

sentences.en: So Honecker actually opposes some of the opening up that Ulbricht does in the 60s, when he genuinely sits down with some youth leaders and says,
sentences.zh: 所以昂纳克实际上反对乌布利希在60年代所做的一些开放举措，当时他真诚地坐下来与一些青年领袖交谈并说，

sentences.en: well, why is it that you're bored with our regime?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么你们会对我们的政权感到厌烦？

sentences.en: Why are people leaving the free German youth?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们要离开自由德国青年团？

sentences.en: And then it's trying to open up by allowing a bit more Western music in, for example, and other things.
sentences.zh: 然后他试图通过允许更多西方音乐进入，例如，以及其他事情来开放。

sentences.en: And Honecker at that point is opposed to it.
sentences.zh: 而昂纳克在那个时候是反对它的。

sentences.en: And then it almost turns around on its head when Ulbricht is ousted for being too old,
sentences.zh: 随后，当乌布利希因年事已高、过于固执、好为人师，基本上总是试图教导东德人该如何生活而被罢免时，局势几乎发生了逆转。

sentences.en: too stubborn, too lectury, basically constantly trying to tell East Germans how to live their lives.
sentences.zh: 太固执，太爱说教，基本上总是试图教导东德人该如何生活。

sentences.en: And Honecker comes in and presents himself as the fresh breath of air who, you know, will bring in reforms and create a new country.
sentences.zh: 昂纳克上台后，将自己塑造成一股清新的空气，你知道，他会带来改革并建立一个新国家。

sentences.en: Because it's not just jeans, is it?
sentences.zh: 因为这不仅仅是牛仔裤的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: It's also Dean Reed, the Red Elvis, who's an American enthusiast for communism, who comes over and it becomes that kind of Elvis, great rock and roll star.
sentences.zh: 还有“红色猫王”迪恩·里德，他是一位热衷于共产主义的美国人，他来到这里，成为了那种猫王式的、伟大的摇滚明星。

sentences.en: Yeah, he suited Honecker perfectly.
sentences.zh: 是的，他非常适合昂纳克。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got this kind of brash, brash, handsome American with the, you know, great flashy smile who comes along and sings Western music and country songs and things,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你拥有这样一个轻浮、轻浮、英俊的美国人，带着你知道的那种灿烂耀眼的笑容，他来到这里，唱着西方音乐、乡村歌曲之类的东西，

sentences.en: things that look and sound like the West does to sort of East Germans.
sentences.zh: 那些在东德人看来，听起来就像是西方的东西。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he's a convinced communist and has been sort of touring the Soviet Union and become a huge star there.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他是一位坚定的共产主义者，曾在苏联巡回演出，并在那里成为了超级巨星。

sentences.en: And it is kind of ideologically reliable, if you will.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你愿意的话，他在意识形态上是可靠的。

sentences.en: So he settles down in East Germany, he marries an East German woman and becomes kind of Honecker's pet cowboy, if you will, to some extent,
sentences.zh: 所以他在东德定居下来，娶了一位东德妻子，在某种程度上成为了昂纳克的“宠物牛仔”，如果你愿意这么说的话，

sentences.en: by projecting a Western image, but doing it in a communist way.
sentences.zh: 通过投射一种西方形象，但以共产主义的方式来做。

sentences.en: Since Tom's brought some music, are they called the Pudys?
sentences.zh: 既然汤姆带了一些音乐，他们叫“普迪乐队”（Pudys）吗？

sentences.en: How would you call them?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么称呼他们？

sentences.en: Yeah, Pudys.
sentences.zh: 是的，普迪乐队。

sentences.en: P-U-H-D-Y-S.
sentences.zh: P-U-H-D-Y-S.

sentences.en: The Pudys.
sentences.zh: 普迪乐队。

sentences.en: And they're the biggest East German band.
sentences.zh: 他们是东德最大的乐队。

sentences.en: Massive.
sentences.zh: 非常庞大。

sentences.en: And if I went to Leipzig now and started chatting to people about the Pudys, they'd know who I was talking about.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在去莱比锡，开始和人们聊起普迪乐队，他们会知道我在说什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're still around.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们依然活跃。

sentences.en: They still give concerts to thousands of people now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在仍然为成千上万的人举办音乐会。

sentences.en: I mean, the kind of lineup has changed a little bit over the years, but they're still going.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多年来阵容确实发生了一些变化，但他们依然在坚持。

sentences.en: So the point of those bands is they're not covering Western songs.
sentences.zh: 所以这些乐队的重点是，他们不翻唱西方歌曲。

sentences.en: They're doing their own songs in German and they're not tainted by imperialist capitalism.
sentences.zh: 他们用德语创作自己的歌曲，而且没有受到帝国主义资本主义的玷污。

sentences.en: Forward to the future with Comrade Honecker.
sentences.zh: 与昂纳克同志一起迈向未来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Absolute smash hit.
sentences.zh: 绝对的超级热门。

sentences.en: No, they are an interesting one, actually, because they started off playing Western music as cover songs, as many GDR bands did in sort of just pubs and village halls
sentences.zh: 不，他们其实很有趣，因为他们刚开始时和许多东德乐队一样，在酒吧和乡村大厅里翻唱西方音乐，

sentences.en: and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的地方。

sentences.en: And then the local Stasi got a bit annoyed with that because they were so effective, for lack of a better word,
sentences.zh: 后来当地的史塔西（Stasi）对此感到有些恼火，因为他们太有效了，用词不当的话，

sentences.en: and creating a kind of exuberant atmosphere that they got young people up dancing and it was incredibly rowdy and they were unhappy with that.
sentences.zh: 他们营造了一种极其热烈的氛围，让年轻人跳起舞来，场面非常喧闹，史塔西对此很不满。

sentences.en: So they told them they can't play anymore and banned them from public appearances.
sentences.zh: 于是他们告诉乐队不能再表演了，并禁止他们公开露面。

sentences.en: And the Pudys actually, to their credit, went back and said, well, what is it that we need to do to try and please you so much that we can play again?
sentences.zh: 而普迪乐队，值得称赞的是，他们回去后说，好吧，我们需要做些什么才能让你们满意，从而让我们能再次表演？

sentences.en: And the authorities said to them, if you write your own songs rather than covering Western songs and you play them in German, absolutely fine, go back.
sentences.zh: 当局告诉他们，如果你们创作自己的歌曲而不是翻唱西方歌曲，并且用德语演唱，那就完全没问题，回去吧。

sentences.en: And so they kind of stayed with their heroes in the West, like Uriah Heep, for example, you know, that entire era, style-wise, but wrote their own German lyrics to go with it.
sentences.zh: 于是他们保留了西方偶像的风格，比如像尤拉·希普（Uriah Heep）那样，你知道，那种时代的风格，但配上了他们自己创作的德语歌词。

sentences.en: And that worked so well.
sentences.zh: 这招非常奏效。

sentences.en: They were really, really popular, both East and West Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们在东德和西德都非常、非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: They actually played concerts in West Germany as well and became one of the most, the most successful band in the GDr.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至在西德举办过音乐会，并成为了东德最成功的乐队之一。

sentences.en: So they're influenced by Western bands.
sentences.zh: 所以他们受到了西方乐队的影响。

sentences.en: And that raises a bigger question, which is, if you were there in East Berlin or wherever, Karl-Marx-Stadt or in East Germany, I mean, do you get West German TV?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个更大的问题，那就是，如果你当时身处东柏林，或者卡尔·马克思城，或者东德的任何地方，你能收看到西德电视吗？

sentences.en: Do you get West German radio?
sentences.zh: 你能收听到西德广播吗？

sentences.en: Do you get, so are you conscious of everything that's going on or are you living in a little prison, not knowing that this is happening?
sentences.zh: 你能吗？所以你是对正在发生的一切了如指掌，还是生活在一个小监狱里，不知道外面发生了什么？

sentences.en: Both to some extent.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上两者皆有。

sentences.en: I mean, you get West German TV and radio almost everywhere in the GDR,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在东德几乎到处都能收看到西德电视和广播，

sentences.en: apart from what was dubbed the Valley of the Clueless in Saxony, where you couldn't guess it.
sentences.zh: 除了萨克森州那个被称为“无知之谷”的地方，那里收不到。

sentences.en: Some of my family are from there, and they joke that they still live in the Valley of the Clueless.
sentences.zh: 我的一些家人就来自那里，他们开玩笑说他们依然生活在“无知之谷”。

sentences.en: But other than that, it was very possible and very commonly done.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，这非常可行，而且非常普遍。

sentences.en: Like the authorities themselves reckon that the vast, vast majority of people watch Western TV and listen to Western radio.
sentences.zh: 当局自己也认为，绝大多数人都在看西德电视、听西德广播。

sentences.en: And to the point, actually, where they adapted their own programming, if there was something, you know, like a crowd plays on in the West,
sentences.zh: 甚至到了这种程度，他们会调整自己的节目安排，如果西边有什么节目，你知道，比如大众播放的节目，

sentences.en: they'd kind of make sure that what they wanted people to see wouldn't be on at the same time, because they knew that people would watch like West German TV.
sentences.zh: 他们会确保他们想让人们看的内容不会在同一时间播出，因为他们知道人们会去看西德电视。

sentences.en: So it was commonly known that that was a thing that people did.
sentences.zh: 所以大家都知道这是人们会做的事情。

sentences.en: And you were also legally allowed to play and listen to Western music in the country, so long as you follow the ratio of 50 to 60.
sentences.zh: 而且在东德，只要遵循50比60的比例，在法律上是允许播放和收听西方音乐的。

sentences.en: So it had to be 60% music, either from East Germany or the Eastern Bloc.
sentences.zh: 所以必须有60%的音乐来自东德或东方集团。

sentences.en: So it's like France.
sentences.zh: 所以就像法国一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In many ways, you could say that.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，你可以这么说。

sentences.en: But the thing, I mean, the thing is, in the 60s and 70s, there is a kind of consumer society developing in East Germany.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，在60年代和70年代，东德正在发展一种消费社会。

sentences.en: So they have more fridges by what's the figure?
sentences.zh: 所以他们的冰箱更多了，数字是多少来着？

sentences.en: By 1970, 56.4% of households had a fridge, as against West Germany's 28%.
sentences.zh: 到1970年，56.4%的家庭拥有冰箱，而西德只有28%。

sentences.en: There are holidays.
sentences.zh: 还有假期。

sentences.en: So you have 18 days holiday a year.
sentences.zh: 所以你每年有18天的假期。

sentences.en: And famously, you have the Trabant.
sentences.zh: 还有著名的卫星牌汽车（Trabant）。

sentences.en: So tell us about the Trabant, which is kind of the ultimate symbol, really, of East Germany, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那么给我们讲讲卫星牌汽车吧，它实际上是东德的终极象征，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: And it's become a symbol of how decrepit the socialist system is, because people looked at them kind of rolling over the border in 1989 and stinking and smitten.
sentences.zh: 它已经成为了社会主义制度衰败的象征，因为人们看到它们在1989年滚过边境时，又臭又破。

sentences.en: So these are cars made in.
sentences.zh: 所以这些车是在哪里制造的？

sentences.en: Yeah, indeed.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: Like two-stroke, little two-stroke cars,
sentences.zh: 就像二冲程，小型的二冲程汽车，

sentences.en: which were terribly outdated, really, by the end of the GDR in 1989.
sentences.zh: 到1989年东德结束时，它们确实已经非常过时了。

sentences.en: But when they first introduced them, they were actually quite modern and decent cars.
sentences.zh: 但当它们刚推出时，其实是相当现代且体面的汽车。

sentences.en: They were sort of modelled on the same design principles as the Triumph Herald in Britain.
sentences.zh: 它们的设计原则在某种程度上模仿了英国的凯旋先驱（Triumph Herald）。

sentences.en: And they look quite stylish, the early ones, when you look at them.
sentences.zh: 当你回头看时，早期的款式看起来相当时尚。

sentences.en: People were quite happy with them.
sentences.zh: 人们对它们相当满意。

sentences.en: The problem was that they didn't get developed any further.
sentences.zh: 问题在于它们没有得到进一步的发展。

sentences.en: So basically, you ended up with the same car model that people were driving in the 1960s, still kind of pretty much the only affordable model in the 1980s,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你最终得到的还是人们在60年代驾驶的同一款车型，在80年代它依然是唯一负担得起的车型，

sentences.en: still on a two-stroke engine, which was just, you know, outdated and just a kind of slightly improved model from the previous one, for which you had to wait a long time.
sentences.zh: 依然使用二冲程发动机，这简直是，你知道，过时了，而且只是比前一款稍微改进了一点，你还得等很长时间才能买到。

sentences.en: You had to apply for it years in advance.
sentences.zh: 你必须提前几年申请。

sentences.en: So people looked after these cars and they had them.
sentences.zh: 所以人们很爱护这些车，并且拥有它们。

sentences.en: And I think it's worth pointing out that car ownership is nearly the same in East Germany as it is in many Western countries, on a par with Britain.
sentences.zh: 我认为值得指出的是，东德的汽车拥有率与许多西方国家几乎相同，与英国持平。

sentences.en: But people just didn't update them.
sentences.zh: 但人们只是没有更新它们。

sentences.en: They couldn't because they couldn't get kind of new car models from anywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们无法更新，因为他们从任何地方都买不到新车型。

sentences.en: And the regime, I don't think, recognised just how car-loving the German people are on the whole and didn't make that the focus, but focused on other things,
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为当时的政权意识到德国人民总体上是多么热爱汽车，并没有把这作为重点，而是关注了其他事情，

sentences.en: like fridges that became the flagship sort of figure that they would constantly trump as well, that they'd temporarily overtake them.
sentences.zh: 比如冰箱，它成为了他们不断吹嘘的旗舰数据，他们暂时超过了西德。

sentences.en: And gold medals in the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 还有奥运会金牌。

sentences.en: And that, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有那个。

sentences.en: So the sporting thing, that kicks in in the late 60s.
sentences.zh: 所以体育方面，是从60年代末开始发力的。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, from the time really when East Germany gets its own national team.
sentences.zh: 是的，真正从东德拥有自己的国家队开始。

sentences.en: For a while, they had to sort of form one all-German team together with the West Germans, which must have been an interesting diplomatic exercise in itself.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，他们不得不与西德人组成一支全德代表队，这本身一定是一次有趣的外交演习。

sentences.en: But once they've got their own, they're really using that to try and create kind of like a national spirit, if you will.
sentences.zh: 但一旦他们有了自己的队伍，他们就真的利用这一点来试图建立一种民族精神，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: So a lot of time, money and thought goes into how to create the sporting success.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时间、金钱和心思都花在了如何创造体育成就上。

sentences.en: And so the stereotype is that they're pumping particularly women with steroids.
sentences.zh: 所以刻板印象是他们给运动员，特别是女性运动员注射类固醇。

sentences.en: And so you have all these kind of bearded women with huge muscles who are chucking shot puts out of the stadium.
sentences.zh: 于是你看到了所有这些长着胡子、肌肉发达的女性，在体育场里投掷铅球。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I mean, they did.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 他们确实做了。

sentences.en: And you can really see that in the records that are still there.
sentences.zh: 你真的可以在至今仍存的记录中看到这一点。

sentences.en: There is no way of getting around that, especially as they identified that if you give steroids
sentences.zh: 这是无法回避的，特别是他们发现如果你给女性注射类固醇，

sentences.en: to women early when they're still in their teens, it permanently alters their physique.
sentences.zh: 在她们十几岁时，这会永久改变她们的体格。

sentences.en: So you can kind of temporarily stop giving them the steroids and they will still perform better in the actual competitions than without them.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以暂时停止给她们注射类固醇，她们在实际比赛中的表现仍然会比不注射时更好。

sentences.en: So this happened and it really permanently damaged the female athletes that were involved in these prograMs.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况确实发生了，并且确实对参与这些项目的女性运动员造成了永久性的伤害。

sentences.en: So it's an interesting story, isn't it, with East Germany?
sentences.zh: 所以东德的故事很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because your book, your pains to sort of say, you've got an extraordinary rate of kind of gender equality.
sentences.zh: 因为你的书竭力想要说明，你们拥有非凡的性别平等率。

sentences.en: So more women working than in most comparable Western countries.
sentences.zh: 所以工作的女性比大多数可比的西方国家都要多。

sentences.en: You have the paid holidays, which Tom mentioned.
sentences.zh: 你有汤姆提到的带薪假期。

sentences.en: You have the consumer society and you still have people who are quite idealistic.
sentences.zh: 你有消费社会，而且你仍然有一些相当理想主义的人。

sentences.en: And yes, on the other side of the equation, as it were, you have the regime that is pumping the athletes full of steroids, but you also have, for example, the Stasi.
sentences.zh: 是的，在等式的另一边，正如人们所说，你有给运动员注射类固醇的政权，但你也有，例如，史塔西。

sentences.en: So the image that most of our listeners, I guess, will have of East Germany is a society in which you're being spied on the whole time.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们大多数听众对东德的印象是一个你时刻被监视的社会。

sentences.en: And it's very repressive.
sentences.zh: 而且非常压抑。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been to the Stasi Museum in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我去过柏林的史塔西博物馆。

sentences.en: And lots of our listeners probably have, where they've got sort of examples of cameras in trees and cameras hidden in, I don't know, cars or something.
sentences.zh: 很多听众可能也去过，那里有藏在树里的摄像头，还有藏在，我不知道，汽车或其他什么东西里的摄像头。

sentences.en: And everybody is watching everybody else.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在监视其他人。

sentences.en: And do you think that latter image is overstated?
sentences.zh: 你认为后一种形象被夸大了吗？

sentences.en: So in other words, do you think East Germany was a better place than we commonly think in the West?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你认为东德是一个比我们在西方通常认为的更好的地方吗？

sentences.en: Or am I now swinging too far to the other extreme?
sentences.zh: 还是我现在走向了另一个极端？

sentences.en: I think it was a more normal place than people think it is, rather than better, I'd say.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是一个比人们想象中更正常的地方，而不是更好，我会这么说。

sentences.en: It completely, literally, completely depended on who you were, what you made of the state.
sentences.zh: 这完全、确实、完全取决于你是谁，你如何看待这个国家。

sentences.en: I mean, if you were somebody who comes from a working class background, and suddenly all
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你是一个来自工人阶级背景的人，突然间所有的机会都为你敞开了，

sentences.en: those opportunities open up for you, you can go to university, you get paid while you study, you can have children while you study.
sentences.zh: 你可以上大学，学习时有工资拿，学习时还可以生孩子。

sentences.en: Like my mum was at university when I was born.
sentences.zh: 就像我出生时我妈妈正在上大学一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, the way that it worked was you would just put in a larger room, which had a nursery attached to it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它的运作方式是你会被安排在一个更大的房间里，里面附带一个托儿所。

sentences.en: You could take your child literally up to the lecture room, drop them at a childcare centre there, go to the lecture, come back out, pick them back up.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接带着孩子去教室，把他们放在那里的托儿中心，去上课，出来后再把他们接走。

sentences.en: But that all worked, you know, and you kind of never had to worry about the existential things that, like Western working class people worried about, like, you know, the stability
sentences.zh: 但这都行得通，你知道，你永远不必担心西方工人阶级担心的那些生存问题，比如，你知道，工作的稳定性，

sentences.en: of your job, how much you'd earn from one day to the next.
sentences.zh: 你每天能赚多少钱。
