sentences.en: Could you afford your rent?
sentences.zh: 你付得起房租吗？

sentences.en: Could you afford to heat your house?
sentences.zh: 你付得起暖气费吗？

sentences.en: You know, none of that was an issue.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些都不是问题。

sentences.en: And if you were happy to live within this kind of relatively small world that the state set up for you, you could do that without existential fears kind of bearing down on you,
sentences.zh: 如果你乐于生活在国家为你建立的这种相对较小的世界里，你就可以做到这一点，而不会有生存恐惧压在身上，

sentences.en: because all of the basic goods in life were stabilised.
sentences.zh: 因为所有的基本生活物资都是稳定的。

sentences.en: As far as the Stasi goes, people just obviously knew that they were being watched.
sentences.zh: 至于史塔西，人们显然知道他们被监视着。

sentences.en: And this is something that happened to the vast majority of people.
sentences.zh: 这是绝大多数人都会经历的事情。

sentences.en: They knew that the Stasi was around and watched their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们知道史塔西就在身边，监视着他们的生活。

sentences.en: But for the most part, the Stasi didn't really seem to know what it was going to do with the information.
sentences.zh: 但在大多数情况下，史塔西似乎并不知道该如何处理这些信息。

sentences.en: I give an example of my dad in the book where he was basically, it was implied that you shouldn't marry my mother because she had Western relatives.
sentences.zh: 我在书中举了我父亲的例子，基本上，当时暗示他不应该娶我母亲，因为她有西方亲戚。

sentences.en: And he was in a very sensitive area in the army where he dealt with radio signalling, which they didn't want to trust to somebody who had kind of potentially relatives in the
sentences.zh: 他在军队中一个非常敏感的部门工作，处理无线电信号，他们不想信任一个在西方有潜在亲戚的人。

sentences.en: WeSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们只是向他暗示了这一点，并不断说些话，比如，你知道你的岳父母周末又去汉堡了吗？因为

sentences.en: And, you know, they kind of just suggested that to him and kept saying things like, did you know that your parents-in-law had gone to Hamburg again over the weekend because
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道，去探亲之类的？

sentences.en: they were, you know, kind of visiting family or something?
sentences.zh: 他说，当然知道。

sentences.en: And he said, well, of course I do.
sentences.zh: 他们是我的岳父母。

sentences.en: They're my parents-in-law.
sentences.zh: 当然我知道他们去了，你知道，他们只是让他知道他们知道。

sentences.en: Well, of course I know that they went, you know, and they just let him know that they knew.
sentences.zh: 他知道除了他们不会让他接触真正敏感的无线电技术之外，不会有任何后果。

sentences.en: And he knew that nothing would come of it other than the fact that they wouldn't trust him with sort of really sensitive radio technology.
sentences.zh: 但这只是生活的一部分。

sentences.en: But it was just a part of life.
sentences.zh: 我问过他，你知道，我不知道问了多少次，比如，这不困扰你吗？

sentences.en: And I've asked him, you know, I don't know how many times, like, did that not bother you?
sentences.zh: 他们知道关于你的一切。

sentences.en: They knew everything about you.
sentences.zh: 在某个地方有一整份档案，他甚至没看过，也不想看，因为他说他知道里面写了什么。

sentences.en: There's a whole file somewhere that he hasn't even looked at and doesn't want to look at because he says he knows what's in it.
sentences.zh: 有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: What's the point?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这只是人们必须面对的生活事实。

sentences.en: You know, this is kind of just a fact of life that people dealt with, I think.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是《德国八三年》（Deutschland 83）的世界，一部关于一名东德人去西方进行渗透的精彩剧集。

sentences.en: Because that's the world of Deutschland 83, brilliant drama about an East German who goes to the West to kind of infiltrate.
sentences.zh: 这就是《德国八三年》的世界，一部关于一名东德人去西方进行渗透的精彩剧集。

sentences.en: And I suppose that's the other thing that people in the West would know about East Germany is it's kind of outsized role that it plays in spy dramas, all those kind of things.
sentences.zh: 我想西方人对东德的另一个印象，就是它在间谍剧等各类作品中扮演的那种超乎寻常的角色。

sentences.en: And the idea of the Stasi as incredibly effective.
sentences.zh: 以及斯塔西（东德国家安全部）那种令人难以置信的高效形象。

sentences.en: And it's also its foreign mission.
sentences.zh: 还有它的对外使命。

sentences.en: So what is it?
sentences.zh: 那么，它到底是什么？

sentences.en: Markus Wulff?
sentences.zh: 马库斯·沃尔夫？

sentences.en: The man without face.
sentences.zh: 那个“无面人”。

sentences.en: The model for Carla in the Carré novels.
sentences.zh: 勒卡雷小说中卡拉的原型。

sentences.en: That in that sense, the impression of East Germany is actually, it's quite an impressive state that it's a significant player, a significant actor in the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，东德给人的印象确实是一个相当令人瞩目的国家，它是冷战中一个重要的参与者，一个重要的角色。

sentences.en: But at the same time, the impression I get from your book is that the blue jeans, the fridges almost serves as a kind of sugar rush for people in East Germany.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，从你的书中我得到的印象是，蓝色牛仔裤、冰箱这些东西，对东德人来说几乎就像是一种糖分带来的短暂兴奋。

sentences.en: And when that starts to crash, that is a problem for these Germans because basically they're starting to run out of money.
sentences.zh: 而当这种兴奋开始消退时，对这些德国人来说就成了问题，因为基本上他们的钱快花光了。

sentences.en: So you have this as early as 1977, this crisis in sourcing coffee, which is incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 所以早在1977年，你就有了这种咖啡采购危机，这可是极其重要的。

sentences.en: Eric's brew and Muckerfuck, which who knows what that means?
sentences.zh: “埃里克的咖啡”和“Muckerfuck”，谁知道那是什么意思？

sentences.en: I said that very carefully, which is good.
sentences.zh: 我刚才说得很小心，这很好。

sentences.en: But it doesn't sound good.
sentences.zh: 但听起来不太好。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a kind of, what is it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这到底是什么？

sentences.en: It's kind of basically dust and shavings.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是些粉末和碎屑。

sentences.en: Chickory, apparently, is I think the basis of it.
sentences.zh: 显然，我想它是以菊苣为基础的。

sentences.en: And it's horrible.
sentences.zh: 而且味道很糟糕。

sentences.en: And reading about the coffee crisis, actually, it sounds quite significant.
sentences.zh: 读到关于咖啡危机的内容时，确实觉得这相当重要。

sentences.en: Coffee presumably is quite important.
sentences.zh: 咖啡大概真的很重要吧。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，德国人确实喜欢喝咖啡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, and this is something I tried to get that across in the book.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这也是我在书中试图传达的东西。

sentences.en: This is something that was associated with post-war stability, having coffee ready and available to you at all times.
sentences.zh: 这与战后的稳定息息相关，即随时随地都能喝到咖啡。

sentences.en: It's like a little comfort blanket.
sentences.zh: 就像一条小小的安抚毯。

sentences.en: You know, whatever happens.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论发生什么。

sentences.en: I suppose it's the equivalent to tea.
sentences.zh: 我想这相当于茶吧。

sentences.en: You know, people say, like, I'll just put the kettle on and everything will be fine in
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们会说，我烧壶水，一切都会好起来的，在

sentences.en: Britain.
sentences.zh: 英国。

sentences.en: I think the equivalent to that in Germany is coffee, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想在德国，咖啡就相当于那个地位。

sentences.en: And when that wasn't available, just imagine tea wasn't available in Britain.
sentences.zh: 当没有咖啡的时候，试想一下如果英国没有茶了。

sentences.en: You know, people would freak out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们会抓狂的。

sentences.en: And it's the same sort of thing, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是一回事。

sentences.en: And the regime notices them.
sentences.zh: 而政权也注意到了这一点。

sentences.zh: 那是矿井里的金丝雀吗？

sentences.en: So in the 80s, is there a sense that the economy in East Germany is starting to run down relative to the West?
sentences.zh: 那么在80年代，是否有一种感觉，即东德的经济相对于西方开始走下坡路了？

sentences.en: And are East Germans becoming resentful of that?
sentences.zh: 东德人是否开始对此感到不满？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, their problem is that they're trying to create a socialist society.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的问题在于他们试图建立一个社会主义社会。

sentences.en: So basically a society where everyone has enough of everything, but nothing luxurious or kind of on top of that.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上是一个每个人都有足够生活必需品，但没有奢侈品或额外享受的社会。

sentences.en: So you have things like rent, food, holidays, all of those kinds of basic things are all subsidized to a point where they are very, very easily affordable and people still have
sentences.zh: 所以你有房租、食品、假期这些基本的东西，它们都被补贴到非常、非常容易负担的程度，人们仍然有

sentences.en: lots of money left over to do things.
sentences.zh: 很多钱剩下可以做别的事情。

sentences.en: And then they can't buy anything with that money.
sentences.zh: 然后他们却没法用这些钱买到任何东西。

sentences.en: So that was, you know, they look at their Western relatives and the Western relatives don't tell
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们看着西方的亲戚，而西方的亲戚不会告诉

sentences.en: them that they're struggling to pay the rent next month, but they're wearing a pair of jeans, you know?
sentences.zh: 他们自己下个月还在为付房租发愁，但他们穿着牛仔裤，你懂吗？

sentences.en: And so I think you get a very, very slanted image in East Germany as to what the West is like, because you view it through this very narrow lens of Western television.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你在东德会得到一个非常、非常片面的西方形象，因为你是通过西方电视这个非常狭窄的镜头来看待它的。

sentences.en: And Honegger is trying to do both.
sentences.zh: 而昂纳克正试图两者兼顾。

sentences.en: He's trying to keep this welfare state that people are used to, which is incredibly expensive.
sentences.zh: 他试图维持人们习惯的那种福利国家制度，这极其昂贵。

sentences.en: You know, free education as well, all the way through to university, all of that's happening.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有免费教育，一直到大学，所有这些都在进行。

sentences.en: If you're an adult and your employer looks at you and thinks, actually, you're a bit too clever for the position that you're doing, don't you want to do something else?
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个成年人，你的雇主看着你，觉得你其实比你现在做的职位要聪明得多，你不想做点别的吗？

sentences.en: They can send you back to university, even at an adult age, and you're getting that paid for.
sentences.zh: 他们可以把你送回大学，即使是成年以后，而且费用由国家承担。

sentences.en: So all of that's happening.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都在发生。

sentences.en: And at the same time, Honegger is now trying to give people, you know, TVs, color TVs and radios and later Walkmans, you know, in the 80s and all of those stereo things for people
sentences.zh: 与此同时，昂纳克现在试图给人们提供电视、彩色电视、收音机，后来还有随身听，你知道，在80年代，还有所有那些让人们

sentences.en: to have at home.
sentences.zh: 在家里使用的立体声设备。

sentences.en: All of these things that in the West, only a small portion of the population can actually afford
sentences.zh: 所有这些在西方只有一小部分人口真正负担得起的东西，

sentences.en: but it looks to people because they see the adverts and they listen to their relatives in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 但对东德人来说，因为他们看到了广告，听到了他们在西方的亲戚的描述，

sentences.en: It looks to people as though everybody has it.
sentences.zh: 看起来好像每个人都有。

sentences.en: And you can't have both of these things by definition.
sentences.zh: 而根据定义，你不可能两者兼得。

sentences.en: You can't have a society that's got everything for everyone and then luxury on top of that for everyone as well.
sentences.zh: 你不可能拥有一个既能为每个人提供一切，又能为每个人提供额外奢侈品的社会。

sentences.en: This just doesn't work economically.
sentences.zh: 这在经济上是行不通的。

sentences.en: And Honegger overstretches himself massively and they find that out in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 昂纳克大大地透支了自己，他们在20世纪80年代发现了这一点。

sentences.en: But even at that point in the 80s, so when they've cheap oil deliveries on which they've relied from the Soviet Union have been cut, they're running into massive economic probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但即使在80年代那个时候，当他们依赖的苏联廉价石油供应被切断时，他们陷入了巨大的经济问题。

sentences.en: East Germany has at this point existed for about 35 years.
sentences.zh: 东德此时已经存在了大约35年。

sentences.en: So it's looking forward to its 40th anniversary.
sentences.zh: 所以它正期待着40周年纪念。

sentences.en: There are an awful lot of people who are now alive who have known nothing but East Germany.
sentences.zh: 现在有很多人除了东德之外一无所知。

sentences.en: You know, you were four in that story that Tom told, but there are a lot of people who would have been older than you who were at school who take East Germany for granted.
sentences.zh: 你知道，汤姆讲的那个故事里你当时四岁，但有很多人比你大，他们在学校里就把东德视为理所当然。

sentences.en: And the regime is also creating, I mean, one of the things I find fascinating is they're creating a separate East German historic identity based on Martin Luther and on Prussia
sentences.zh: 而且政权也在创造，我的意思是，我发现最迷人的一点是，他们正在创造一个基于马丁·路德和普鲁士的独立的东德历史认同，

sentences.en: and on a sort of separate history.
sentences.zh: 以及一种某种程度上独立的历史。

sentences.en: So is there a point there in the 1980s where most people genuinely believe East Germany is its own thing?
sentences.zh: 那么在80年代，是否有那么一个时刻，大多数人真的相信东德是一个独立的实体？

sentences.en: It's not just some sort of mutilated appendix of a greater Germany, but it's its own thing with its own history, its own culture, and it will last for generations.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是大德国的一个残缺的附庸，而是一个拥有自己历史、自己文化、并将持续几代人的独立实体。

sentences.en: Do you think there are people who genuinely think that?
sentences.zh: 你认为有人真的这么想吗？

sentences.en: Most people did.
sentences.zh: 大多数人是这样想的。

sentences.en: I mean, if you speak to people even about 1989, there's a tiny minority who say now that they knew that the state was going to collapse and Germany was going to reunify.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你和人们谈论1989年，现在只有极少数人说他们当时就知道国家会崩溃，德国会统一。

sentences.en: But the vast majority of people thought that, you know, there were two German states for the foreseeable future.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数人认为，在可预见的未来，会有两个德国国家。

sentences.en: And you see that even in the conversations between the West German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在西德总理赫尔穆特·科尔和

sentences.en: Irik Onyka, that they're working towards kind of what they call a neighbourly relationship
sentences.zh: 埃里希·昂纳克之间的对话中看到这一点，他们正致力于建立所谓的睦邻关系，

sentences.en: between the two states, because they both accept at this point that for the foreseeable future, there will be two German states.
sentences.zh: 因为他们双方在这一点上都接受，在可预见的未来，将会有两个德国国家。

sentences.en: East Germany has got its own, you know, citizenship, for example.
sentences.zh: 东德有自己的公民身份，例如。

sentences.en: There is through sport to some extent as well, a kind of East German identity on the world stage.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，通过体育，在世界舞台上也有了一种东德认同。

sentences.en: You've got your own team, basically, that you look up to.
sentences.zh: 你基本上有你支持的自己的队伍。

sentences.en: So I think that there was certainly a sense that maybe it was still one nation, but it would live in two separate states for now.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，肯定有一种感觉，也许它仍然是一个民族，但目前将生活在两个独立的国家中。

sentences.en: I mean, Katja, the transcripts of the dialogue between Eric Onyka and Chancellor Kohl of West
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，卡佳，埃里希·昂纳克和西德总理科尔之间的对话记录，

sentences.en: Germany, and you reproduce some of it.
sentences.zh: 你摘录了一些。

sentences.en: I mean, it's magnificent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太精彩了。

sentences.en: So Onyka, phoning up Kohl, yes, hello?
sentences.zh: 所以昂纳克给科尔打电话，喂，你好？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Kohl saying, yes, this is Kohl.
sentences.zh: 科尔说，是的，我是科尔。

sentences.en: Good day.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Good day, Chancellor.
sentences.zh: 你好，总理。

sentences.en: This is Onyka.
sentences.zh: 我是昂纳克。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Good day, General Secretary.
sentences.zh: 你好，总书记。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Excellent, I would like to say.
sentences.zh: 我想说，非常好。

sentences.en: If only the weather was a little better.
sentences.zh: 要是天气再好一点就好了。

sentences.en: How is the weather over there?
sentences.zh: 那边天气怎么样？

sentences.en: Misty?
sentences.zh: 有雾？

sentences.en: Fog?
sentences.zh: 雾气？

sentences.en: I mean, this is almost British level.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是英国级别的。

sentences.en: Conversation.
sentences.zh: 对话。

sentences.en: I mean, it's quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很有趣。

sentences.en: So it all seems so normal.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切看起来如此正常。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly it.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: That's what I was trying to get to with that, is that it was just normal.
sentences.zh: 这就是我试图通过这一点表达的，它就是很正常。

sentences.en: And I mean, Kohl, obviously, once he gets a chance in 1989, styles himself as the unification chancellor.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，科尔显然在1989年有机会时，将自己塑造成了统一总理。

sentences.en: But he certainly had a fairly workable, amicable relationship with Onyka.
sentences.zh: 但他确实与昂纳克保持着相当可行、友好的关系。

sentences.en: You suppose when they first met in Moscow at Andropov's funeral the first time, and then for their first formal meeting at Chernenko's.
sentences.zh: 你以为他们第一次在莫斯科安德罗波夫的葬礼上见面时，以及后来在契尔年科的葬礼上第一次正式会面时。

sentences.en: But the first time they met, he's supposed to have said to him, you know, if we speak in dialect, then people won't understand what we're saying.
sentences.zh: 但他们第一次见面时，据说他对他说，你知道，如果我们用方言交谈，人们就听不懂我们在说什么了。

sentences.en: You can't be eavesdropped upon, because their birthplaces are only 100 kilometres apart, which is quite remarkable.
sentences.zh: 你无法被窃听，因为他们的出生地相距仅100公里，这非常了不起。

sentences.en: You know, so they do have this unlikely sort of relatively personal relationship with one another, where there is, I think, a degree of goodwill on both sides to try and make
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以他们确实有一种不太可能的、相对私人的关系，我认为双方都有一定程度的善意，试图让

sentences.en: this work.
sentences.zh: 这一切行得通。

sentences.en: So 1989 comes, and the description you gave, which I read so beautifully, impersonating you at the beginning of this.
sentences.zh: 所以1989年来了，你给出的描述，我在开头模仿你读得那么美。

sentences.en: It's like I was here.
sentences.zh: 就像我当时就在现场一样。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Tell us what happens.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们发生了什么。

sentences.en: So first of all, what happens when your father sees this?
sentences.zh: 首先，当你父亲看到这一切时发生了什么？

sentences.en: What happens to you?
sentences.zh: 你发生了什么？

sentences.en: What's the process?
sentences.zh: 过程是什么？

sentences.en: And then how do you fit that into the broader context of what happens in 1989?
sentences.zh: 然后你如何将其融入1989年发生的更广泛的背景中？

sentences.en: Well, he genuinely got quite frightened when I pointed out all of this kind of mayhem that was happening at the foot of the TV tower.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我指出电视塔脚下发生的所有这些混乱时，他确实感到非常害怕。

sentences.en: Because it was 1989, it was the last day of the Republic, the 7th of October,
sentences.zh: 因为那是1989年，共和国的最后一天，10月7日，

sentences.en: which was a nice sunny day, because it was the day of the Republic, everybody had the day off, and
sentences.zh: 那是一个阳光明媚的日子，因为那是共和国日，每个人都放假，

sentences.en: most families like my own used it to just have a day out.
sentences.zh: 大多数像我家一样的家庭都利用这一天出去玩。

sentences.en: So we chose to go to Berlin and go up the TV tower, which was perhaps bad timing, because
sentences.zh: 所以我们选择去柏林，登上电视塔，这可能时机不对，因为

sentences.en: that's when there was a huge ceremony in Berlin to try and sort of celebrate the last day of the Republic.
sentences.zh: 当时柏林正在举行一场盛大的仪式，试图庆祝共和国的最后一天。

sentences.en: Gorbachev had come along to witness it.
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫也来见证了这一时刻。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, you get mass demonstrations against that at the same time.
sentences.zh: 结果，与此同时，出现了针对这一仪式的群众示威。

sentences.en: And there was no telling whatsoever what the police would do, or the security forces would
sentences.zh: 而且根本无法预料警察或安全部队会做什么，

sentences.en: do, because the authorities were still talking about a Chinese solution to this, meaning the massacre that had happened on Tiananmen Square.
sentences.zh: 因为当局当时还在谈论用“中国方案”来解决这个问题，指的是天安门广场发生的屠杀。

sentences.en: And they're still kind of at least threatening to dangle that into the air, that threat.
sentences.zh: 他们至少还在威胁要抛出这个威胁。

sentences.en: Katja, why the demonstrations?
sentences.zh: 卡佳，为什么会有示威？

sentences.en: And the reason I ask why is because surely at that point, most people in East Germany are better off than they have ever been.
sentences.zh: 我问为什么的原因是，因为在那个时候，东德的大多数人肯定比以往任何时候都过得好。

sentences.en: So much as we look at it from the viewpoint of 2023 and we say, what a ghastly regime, what a terrible place, even though you've made your case about its normality.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管我们从2023年的角度来看，说这是一个多么可怕的政权，多么糟糕的地方，尽管你已经证明了它的正常性。

sentences.en: It's not like they're suddenly terribly badly off.
sentences.zh: 并不是说他们突然过得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: It's not like the regime has suddenly become loads more repressive than it was before.
sentences.zh: 也不是说政权突然变得比以前压迫得多。

sentences.en: What's driving people out onto the streets?
sentences.zh: 是什么驱使人们走上街头？

sentences.en: I think that's part of the problem, is they put people in a position where they are incredibly well-educated.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是问题的一部分，他们把人们置于一个受过极好教育的位置。

sentences.en: I mean, Germany is one of the most widely read societies in the world at that point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，德国在当时是世界上阅读最广泛的社会之一。

sentences.en: People read a lot.
sentences.zh: 人们读很多书。

sentences.en: People are very intelligent because they've been basically well-educated to a much, like they
sentences.zh: 人们非常聪明，因为他们基本上受过良好的教育，就像他们

sentences.en: all take the same schooling to year 10, which is kind of really high quality and there's no streaming as such.
sentences.zh: 都接受同样的教育直到10年级，质量真的很高，而且没有分流。

sentences.en: So you've got a very well-educated, highly politicized, quite comfortable population and confident population who are now saying, why isn't this changing?
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有一个受过良好教育、高度政治化、相当舒适且自信的人群，他们现在在问，为什么这没有改变？

sentences.en: Why can't we have reform?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能进行改革？

sentences.en: Why can't we get a say?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能有发言权？

sentences.en: And this is very, very different from the early years where people just wanted peace, stability
sentences.zh: 这与早年人们只想要和平、稳定，

sentences.en: and wanted to basically just get on with their lives, regardless of what was happening at the top.
sentences.zh: 基本上只想过好自己的生活，而不关心高层发生了什么的情况非常、非常不同。

sentences.en: People accept a high degree of kind of authoritarianism in the West as well under Conrad Adenauer to start with.
sentences.zh: 人们在西方的康拉德·阿登纳统治下，起初也接受了高度的威权主义。

sentences.en: And then you see that developing into protest in the late 60s and early 70s for similar reasons.
sentences.zh: 然后你看到这种情况在60年代末和70年代初因类似原因发展成了抗议。

sentences.en: And nothing changes at the top.
sentences.zh: 高层没有任何改变。

sentences.en: There's no attempt whatsoever to listen to people, to try and bring reforms in.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有尝试去倾听民众的声音，也没有试图进行任何改革。

sentences.en: Honig is at that point quite old and also getting ill.
sentences.zh: 昂纳克当时已经很老了，而且身体状况也在恶化。

sentences.en: So he's increasingly even less likely than he had been to start with to engage with people and to engage with their arguments.
sentences.zh: 所以，他比最初更不可能去接触民众，也不可能去听取他们的意见。

sentences.en: And this is really quite upsetting to a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这对许多人来说确实非常令人沮丧。

sentences.en: I spoke to one man, Wolfgang Walensky, who stood for the Liberal Party in 1989 in the local elections.
sentences.zh: 我采访过一个人，沃尔夫冈·瓦伦斯基，他在1989年的地方选举中代表自由党参选。

sentences.en: And they always had to have like a sort of pre-election discussion with the electorate.
sentences.zh: 他们当时总是要进行某种选前的选民讨论。

sentences.en: And he said it was so hostile.
sentences.zh: 他说现场充满了敌意。

sentences.en: People were just sitting there, even though he wasn't actually part of the ruling Socialist
sentences.zh: 人们就坐在那里，尽管他其实并不是执政的社会主义政党成员。

sentences.en: Party.
sentences.zh: 但他们坐在那里说，听着，我们需要改变。

sentences.en: But they were sitting there and saying, look, we need change.
sentences.zh: 我们需要改革。

sentences.en: We need reform.
sentences.zh: 我们需要在环境问题上做点什么。

sentences.en: We need to do something about the environment.
sentences.zh: 住房依然不足。
